text: All the elements that are more massive than iron were formed by what astronomical phenomenon?
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Recall that elements heavier than iron cannot be formed through fusion in stars due to energy constraints.
Identify that supernovae are explosive events that occur at the end of a massive star's life cycle.
Recognize that during a supernova, the extreme temperatures and pressures allow for the synthesis of heavier elements.
Eliminate other options by noting that novae and white dwarfs do not produce elements heavier than iron, and black holes do not create elements.

text: What is the term for the minimum distance from a planet at which a satellite can remain intact, without being torn apart by gravitational forces?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of gravitational forces acting on a satellite.
Understand that there is a threshold distance where these forces can cause structural failure.
Recall the specific term used in astrophysics to describe this threshold distance.
Conclude that the term for this minimum distance is the Roche Limit.

text: Which of the following molecules is NOT known to destroy ozone molecules in our stratosphere? W) Chloroflurocarbons X) Chlorine Y) Bromine Z) Argon
explainAnswer: Identify the substances listed in the options and their known effects on ozone.
Recall that chlorofluorocarbons, chlorine, and bromine are all known to contribute to ozone depletion.
Recognize that argon is a noble gas and does not react with ozone or contribute to its destruction.
Conclude that the molecule that does not destroy ozone is argon.

text: Galena is a sulfide ore of what metal element?
explainAnswer: Identify that galena is a mineral commonly known as a sulfide ore.
Recall that sulfide ores are typically associated with specific metals.
Recognize that galena is primarily known as the main ore of lead.
Conclude that the metal element associated with galena is lead.

text: Identify all of the following four objects around which accretion disks are sometimes present: 1) White dwarfs; 2) Protostars; 3) Stellar mass black holes; 4) Supermassive black holes.
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Understand that accretion disks form when material falls into a gravitational well, which can occur around various astronomical objects.
Recognize that white dwarfs can accumulate material from a companion star, forming an accretion disk.
Identify that protostars are in the early stages of star formation and often have surrounding disks of gas and dust that contribute to their growth.
Acknowledge that both stellar mass black holes and supermassive black holes can attract surrounding matter, leading to the formation of accretion disks as material spirals inwards.

text: As a planet with a circular orbit revolves around a star, how many of its five Lagrangian [lah-GRAHN-jee-in] points will also move?
explainAnswer: Identify the five Lagrangian points in a two-body system, which are L1, L2, L3, L4, and L5.
Understand that Lagrangian points are positions where the gravitational forces and the orbital motion balance.
Recognize that in a circular orbit, the Lagrangian points maintain their positions relative to the two bodies involved.
Conclude that since the planet is in a circular orbit, all five Lagrangian points will move with it as it revolves around the star.

text: When large-scale space has zero curvature, its geometry is referred to by what adjective?
explainAnswer: Understand that curvature in geometry can be classified as positive, negative, or zero.
Recognize that zero curvature indicates a flat geometry.
Recall that in cosmology, a universe with zero curvature is described as 'flat'.
Conclude that the adjective used to describe large-scale space with zero curvature is 'flat'.

text: What is the name given to the end moraine [mohr-AYN] that denotes the farthest advance of glacial ice?
explainAnswer: Identify the term related to glacial features.
Recall the specific types of moraines associated with glaciers.
Determine which moraine represents the furthest advance of a glacier.
Conclude that the name for this moraine is terminal moraine.

text: What structural modification did the United States introduce to enable atmospheric pollutants such as nitrogen and sulfur oxides to be dispersed at higher altitudes?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which relates to environmental science and pollution control.
Consider the methods used to reduce the impact of pollutants on air quality.
Recall the structural modifications made to industrial facilities to improve pollutant dispersion.
Recognize that smokestacks are designed to release emissions at higher altitudes to minimize ground-level pollution.

text: What gas is primarily responsible for the blue coloration of Uranus and Neptune?
explainAnswer: Recall that the color of a planet can be influenced by the gases in its atmosphere.
Identify the primary components of Uranus and Neptune's atmospheres, which include hydrogen and helium.
Research additional gases present in their atmospheres, focusing on trace gases that could affect color.
Recognize that methane absorbs red light and reflects blue light, contributing to the blue appearance of these planets.
Conclude that methane is the gas primarily responsible for the blue coloration of Uranus and Neptune.

text: What cinder cone appeared in 1943 in a Mexican corn field and is one of the most well characterized cinder cone volcanoes?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of cinder cone volcanoes, including their formation and eruption style.
Research significant historical cinder cone eruptions, focusing on the 20th century.
Look for notable eruptions that occurred in Mexico, particularly in agricultural areas.
Cross-reference the details of the eruption with known cinder cone volcanoes to find the one that matches the description.
Confirm that Paricutin is recognized for its well-documented eruption and characteristics.

text: Refracting telescopes have a severe limitation in that each wavelength of light is refracted differently, making it impossible to focus on more than one wavelength of light at a time. What is this type of optical aberration called?
explainAnswer: Identify the phenomenon where different wavelengths of light are refracted at different angles.
Recall the term used to describe optical aberrations caused by this effect.
Recognize that this specific aberration affects the focus of colors in optical instruments.
Conclude that the correct term for this optical issue is chromatic aberration.

text: Identify all of the following three rocks that would be classified as aphanitic [AFF-in-it-ik]: 1) Andesite [ANN-deh-site]; 2) Basalt [bah-SALT]; 3) Diorite.
explainAnswer: Understand that aphanitic rocks are those with a fine-grained texture, meaning their mineral crystals are too small to be seen with the naked eye.
Identify that andesite and basalt are both volcanic rocks that cool quickly, resulting in their fine-grained texture.
Recognize that diorite is an intrusive igneous rock, which cools slowly underground, leading to a coarse-grained texture.
Conclude that andesite and basalt are classified as aphanitic, while diorite is not.

text: Landscapes that have been shaped by the dissolving power of water are said to exhibit what type of topography?
explainAnswer: Identify the key term related to landscapes shaped by water.
Recall the geological processes involved in the dissolution of rock by water.
Recognize that the term for such landscapes is associated with limestone and features like caves and sinkholes.
Conclude that the correct term for this type of topography is 'karst'.

text: What geologic eon extends from around 542 million years ago through the present day?
explainAnswer: Identify the major divisions of geologic time, which include eons, eras, periods, and epochs.
Recall that the Phanerozoic eon is the most recent eon in the geologic time scale.
Note that the Phanerozoic eon began approximately 542 million years ago.
Recognize that the Phanerozoic eon continues to the present day.

text: Decompression melting will occur when the solidus of an ascending mass of rock crosses what thermodynamic boundary?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of decompression melting and its relationship to rock ascent.
Understand that the solidus is the temperature below which a rock is solid and above which it begins to melt.
Recognize that the geotherm represents the temperature gradient of the Earth's interior as it relates to depth.
Determine that decompression melting occurs when the solidus intersects the geotherm during the ascent of the rock.

text: What planet in the solar system is the most dense?
explainAnswer: Research the densities of all the planets in the solar system.
List the planets along with their respective densities.
Compare the densities to identify which planet has the highest value.
Confirm that Earth has the highest density among the planets.

text: The closed universe is a solution of Einstein's equations of general relativity in which the mass density of the Universe exceeds what parameter?
explainAnswer: Understand that the closed universe model relates to the overall geometry of the universe.
Recall that Einstein's equations describe how mass and energy influence the curvature of spacetime.
Identify that critical density is the threshold density that determines the geometry of the universe.
Conclude that in a closed universe, the mass density must exceed this critical density for the universe to curve back on itself.

text: What greenhouse gas has the greatest abundance in the atmosphere?
explainAnswer: Identify the major greenhouse gases present in the atmosphere, such as carbon dioxide, methane, and water vapor.
Research the relative concentrations of these gases in the atmosphere.
Determine which gas has the highest concentration based on your research.
Conclude that water vapor is the most abundant greenhouse gas.

text: Identify all of the following three types of objects that could be considered meteors: 1) Fragments of asteroids; 2) Fragments of comets; 3) Impact debris from Mars.
explainAnswer: Understand that meteors are defined as objects that enter the Earth's atmosphere and produce a visible streak of light.
Recognize that fragments of asteroids can enter the atmosphere and are classified as meteors.
Acknowledge that fragments of comets, when they enter the atmosphere, also create meteors.
Consider that impact debris from Mars can be ejected into space and eventually enter Earth's atmosphere, making it a meteor as well.
Conclude that all three types of objects can be classified as meteors.

text: In what month does light take longest to travel from the Sun to the Earth?
explainAnswer: Understand that the distance from the Sun to the Earth varies throughout the year due to the elliptical shape of Earth's orbit.
Recognize that Earth is farthest from the Sun around early July, known as aphelion.
Know that light takes longer to travel longer distances.
Conclude that in July, when Earth is at aphelion, light takes the longest time to travel from the Sun to the Earth.

text: What type of star must be present prior to a Type One-A supernova?
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Understand that a Type Ia supernova occurs in a binary star system.
Identify that one of the stars in this system must be a white dwarf.
Recognize that the white dwarf accumulates matter from its companion star.
Determine that when the white dwarf reaches a critical mass, it undergoes a thermonuclear explosion, resulting in a Type Ia supernova.

text: What type of nebula is formed as a star ejects ionized gas after its evolution through the asymptotic giant branch phase?
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Identify the stages of stellar evolution, particularly the asymptotic giant branch phase.
Understand that during this phase, stars expand and eject their outer layers.
Recognize that the ejected material becomes ionized due to the intense radiation from the remaining core.
Conclude that the resulting structure is known as a planetary nebula.

text: Crater Lake in Oregon occupies what type of volcanic feature?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of Crater Lake, noting that it is formed in a volcanic setting.
Recall the types of volcanic features, such as craters, calderas, and cones.
Determine that a caldera is formed when a volcano erupts and collapses, creating a large depression.
Confirm that Crater Lake was formed by the collapse of Mount Mazama, which supports it being classified as a caldera.

text: If a slow-moving warm front is followed by a fast- moving cold front, the cold front will sometimes overtake the warm front. When the cold air lifts the warm air entirely aloft, what atmospheric phenomenon results?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of a warm front and a cold front.
Understand that when a cold front overtakes a warm front, it can lift the warm air off the ground.
Recognize that this process leads to the formation of an occluded front.
Eliminate other options based on their definitions and characteristics.

text: A line of brown semicircles on a weather map indicates:
explainAnswer: Understand that weather symbols represent different meteorological phenomena.
Recognize that a dry line is typically depicted by a line of semicircles on weather maps.
Eliminate other options by recalling their typical representations: warm fronts have rounded symbols, cold fronts have triangular symbols, and smog is not represented by a line of semicircles.
Conclude that the line of brown semicircles corresponds to a dry line.

text: What type of lava can be expected to erupt from a shield volcano, like Kilauea?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of shield volcanoes, which typically have broad, gentle slopes.
Understand that shield volcanoes primarily erupt low-viscosity lava.
Recognize that basalt is the type of lava that is low in viscosity and is commonly associated with shield volcanoes.
Eliminate the other options (Andesite, Dacite, Rhyolite) as they are typically associated with more explosive volcanic activity.

text: Which of the following major wind belts occurs between 0 degrees and 30 degrees North latitude?
explainAnswer: Identify the latitude range specified in the question, which is between 0 degrees and 30 degrees North.
Recall the major wind belts and their corresponding latitude ranges.
Recognize that the Northeast trade winds occur specifically in the 0 to 30 degrees North latitude range.
Eliminate other options that do not fit within this latitude range.

text: Which planet in our solar system has a semi-major axis closest to 2 AU?
explainAnswer: Understand that the semi-major axis is the average distance from a planet to the Sun in astronomical units (AU).

Know the semi-major axes of the planets in the solar system: Mercury (0.39 AU), Venus (0.72 AU), Earth (1 AU), Mars (1.52 AU), Jupiter (5.20 AU), Saturn (9.58 AU), Uranus (19.22 AU), and Neptune (30.05 AU).
Identify the planet with a semi-major axis closest to 2 AU by comparing the values.
Determine that Mars, with a semi-major axis of 1.52 AU, is the closest to 2 AU compared to other planets.

text: Which of the following groups of stars exhibits the empirical relationship that luminosity is proportional to mass to the 3.5 power?
explainAnswer: Understand that the relationship between luminosity and mass for stars is described by the mass-luminosity relation.
Recall that for main sequence stars, luminosity is approximately proportional to mass raised to the 3.5 power.
Eliminate other options by noting that giants, supergiants, and white dwarfs do not follow this specific mass-luminosity relationship.
Conclude that the main sequence is the correct group of stars exhibiting this relationship.

text: Which of the following types of olivine has the highest iron content?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical composition of each type of olivine: Forsterite (Mg2SiO4), Fayalite (Fe2SiO4), Monticellite (CaMgSiO4), and Tephroite (Mn2SiO4).
Determine the iron content in each type by looking at the formula; Fayalite contains the highest proportion of iron (Fe).
Compare the iron content in the formulas to see that Fayalite has the most iron compared to the others.

text: Which of the following is closest to the percentage of the ocean area that is represented by continental shelves?
explainAnswer: Understand that continental shelves are the submerged edges of continents and represent a small portion of the ocean area.
Recall that continental shelves typically cover about 7-10% of the total ocean area.
Compare the options given (10, 20, 30, 40) and identify which is closest to the estimated percentage.
Select 10% as the answer since it is the closest to the actual percentage of ocean area represented by continental shelves.

text: What type of faulting is defined by strike-slip offset along an essentially vertical fault plane?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of different fault types: normal, reverse, thrust, and strike-slip.
Understand that strike-slip faults involve horizontal movement along the fault plane.
Recognize that transcurrent faults are synonymous with strike-slip faults and involve vertical fault planes.
Eliminate options that do not fit the definition of strike-slip offset, such as normal, reverse, and thrust faults.
Conclude that the correct answer is transcurrent, as it specifically refers to strike-slip faults.

text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about upwelling?
choices: It is associated with good fishing
Water that rises to the surface as a result of upwelling is typically colder and richer in nutrients
It is caused when offshore wind causes surface water to build up along a coastline
It occurs in the open ocean and along coastlines
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of upwelling and what causes it.
Evaluate each statement to determine if it accurately describes upwelling.
Focus on the statement regarding offshore wind and surface water buildup.
Recognize that upwelling is actually caused by offshore winds pushing surface water away, allowing deeper water to rise, not by building up surface water.
Conclude that the identified statement is the one that is NOT true about upwelling.

text: Which of the following is LEAST likely to occur when viewed from mid-northern latitudes in the month of August:
choices: the Moon at apogee on the 1<sup>st</sup> of the month and perigee at the 29<sup>th</sup> of the month
the Moon passing within 5º of Uranus
explainAnswer: Identify the astronomical events mentioned in the choices.
Research the typical positions and movements of the celestial bodies involved during August from mid-northern latitudes.
Evaluate the likelihood of each event occurring based on their positions and the timing of the month.
Determine which event is least likely to occur based on the gathered information.

text: Which of the following best explains why Cepheid variables can be used as standard candles?
choices: Their periods and luminosities are highly correlated
Their absolute luminosities can be calculated by simulating fusion
Their redshifts determine their distance from Earth
They are always found in star-forming nebulae
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of standard candles in astronomy, which are objects with known luminosity used to measure distances.
Recognize that Cepheid variables are a type of star whose brightness varies in a regular cycle.
Identify that the key property of Cepheid variables is the relationship between their pulsation period and their absolute luminosity.
Conclude that this correlation allows astronomers to determine their distance based on observed brightness.

text: According to the Saffir-Simpson scale, a hurricane with maximum sustained winds of 67 meters per second is considered to be what category?
explainAnswer: Understand that the Saffir-Simpson scale categorizes hurricanes based on their maximum sustained wind speeds.
Identify the wind speed thresholds for each category: Category 1 (33-42 m/s), Category 2 (43-49 m/s), Category 3 (50-58 m/s), Category 4 (59-69 m/s), and Category 5 (≥70 m/s).
Compare the given wind speed of 67 m/s to the thresholds.
Determine that 67 m/s falls within the range for Category 4, which is 59-69 m/s.

text: A sedimentary deposit consists of three layers: a base layer of gravel-sized grains, an intermediate layer of sand, and a top layer of silt and other fine particles. Assuming the deposit has not been overturned, what type of grading does the deposit represent?
explainAnswer: Identify the order of the layers in the sedimentary deposit, which are gravel at the bottom, sand in the middle, and silt at the top.
Recognize that in a normal grading, coarser materials are found at the bottom and finer materials at the top.
Confirm that the arrangement of layers follows this pattern, indicating a normal grading.
Eliminate other grading types by understanding their definitions and how they differ from the normal grading observed.

text: What arises in space, thought to be from particle pairs that blink into existence and promptly annihilate?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of particle-antiparticle pairs that spontaneously appear and disappear in a vacuum.
Recognize that this phenomenon is related to quantum field theory.
Understand that the energy associated with these fluctuations is referred to as vacuum energy.
Eliminate the other options based on their definitions and relevance to the concept of vacuum fluctuations.

text: Bauxite, the hydroxide ore of aluminum, is mined primarily from deposits in tropical areas. What process causes these deposits to form?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of bauxite and its formation environment.
Consider the processes that lead to the weathering of rocks in tropical climates.
Eliminate options that do not relate to the weathering of minerals.
Determine that chemical weathering is the process that breaks down rocks and minerals to form bauxite.

text: Which of the following is a fine-grained, typically buff- colored sediment deposited by wind?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of each sediment type listed in the choices.
Recall that loess is a wind-blown sediment that is fine-grained and typically buff-colored.
Eliminate options that do not match the description of being fine-grained and wind-deposited.
Confirm that loess is the only choice that fits all the criteria.

text: Which of the following is NOT true about geothermal gradients?
choices: The gradient beneath continent crust is less steep than under oceanic crust
They are largely determined by the way that pressure and temperature vary in the Earth
The “normal” geothermal gradient in the upper part of Earth is 25<sup>̊</sup>C/km
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions and characteristics of geothermal gradients.
Evaluate each statement in the context of known geological principles.
Compare the geothermal gradients beneath continental and oceanic crusts.
Determine which statement contradicts established knowledge about geothermal gradients.
Select the statement that is NOT true based on your evaluations.

text: Which of the following is LEAST accurate:
choices: at the equator, stars appear to rise and set vertically
all Mira stars are Red Giants
right ascension is analogous to longitude
the Earth is closest to the Sun during December
explainAnswer: Identify the statements and evaluate their accuracy based on astronomical facts.
Recall that the Earth is actually closest to the Sun during early January, not December.
Consider the other statements to verify their accuracy: stars at the equator rise and set vertically, all Mira stars are indeed Red Giants, and right ascension is analogous to longitude.
Conclude that the statement about Earth's proximity to the Sun in December is the least accurate.

text: Which of the following statements is LEAST accurate:
choices: solar eclipses are less common than lunar eclipses
stars that begin their lives with greater mass have longer life-spans
stars in the same constellation are not necessarily at the same distance from Earth
explainAnswer: Identify the statements and evaluate their accuracy based on astronomical principles.
Recall that more massive stars actually have shorter life-spans due to their rapid fuel consumption.

Compare the remaining statements to determine their accuracy: solar eclipses are indeed less common than lunar eclipses, stars in the same constellation can be at varying distances, and M-31 is correctly identified as a galaxy.
Conclude that the statement about massive stars having longer life-spans is the least accurate.

text: In the course of its evolution, what is the main element that has accumulated when helium becomes exhausted in the core of a red giant star?
explainAnswer: Understand that red giant stars undergo nuclear fusion processes in their cores.
Recognize that after helium is exhausted, the core contracts and heats up, allowing for further fusion.
Identify that the primary product of helium fusion is carbon through the triple-alpha process.
Conclude that carbon is the main element that accumulates in the core when helium is exhausted.

text: Coral polyps extract what compound out of seawater to form hard external skeletons?
explainAnswer: Identify the biological process by which coral polyps build their skeletons.
Recognize that coral polyps extract minerals from seawater.
Determine which specific compound is used to form the hard external skeletons.
Conclude that the compound extracted is calcium carbonate.

text: What was the first black hole discovered?
explainAnswer: Identify significant historical discoveries in astronomy.
Research the timeline of black hole discoveries.
Locate the first black hole that was confirmed through observation.
Verify that CYGNUS X-1 was recognized as the first black hole in the 1970s.

text: Place the following three Galilean satellites of Jupiter in increasing order of distance from Jupiter: 1) Europa; 2) Ganymede [GAN-ih-meed]; 3) Io [EYE-oh].
explainAnswer: Identify the distances of each Galilean satellite from Jupiter: Io is the closest, followed by Europa, and Ganymede is the farthest.
List the satellites in order of increasing distance based on the identified distances.
Assign numerical values to the satellites: Io = 1, Europa = 2, Ganymede = 3.
Arrange the satellites in the order of their numerical values to find the correct sequence.

text: The Galápagos Islands consist of a single active volcano among volcanic islands whose ages increase westward. Based on this knowledge, what geologic scenario is creating the islands?
explainAnswer: Identify that the Galápagos Islands are formed from volcanic activity.
Recognize that a hot spot is a location where magma from deep within the Earth's mantle rises to the surface.
Note that the age of the islands increases westward, indicating that the tectonic plate is moving over a stationary hot spot.
Eliminate other options like subduction and sea floor spreading, which do not explain the formation of a chain of islands with increasing age.

text: Place the following three photon emissions from hydrogen in order of increasing wavelength: 1) Electron transition from n = 3 to n = 2; 2) Electronic spin transition from parallel to antiparallel relative to protium nucleus; 3) Electronic transition from n = 2 to n = 1.
explainAnswer: Identify the energy levels involved in each transition: n=3 to n=2, n=2 to n=1, and the electronic spin transition.
Determine the energy difference for each transition using the formula E = -13.6 eV (1/n_final^2 - 1/n_initial^2) for the electronic transitions.
Calculate the corresponding wavelengths using the formula λ = hc/E, where h is Planck's constant and c is the speed of light.
Compare the calculated wavelengths to order them from shortest to longest, which corresponds to increasing wavelength.

text: Identify all of the following three gas giants that are hypothesized to have a layer of liquid metallic hydrogen: 1) Saturn; 2) Uranus: 3) Neptune.
explainAnswer: Recall that gas giants are primarily composed of hydrogen and helium.
Understand that under extreme pressure, hydrogen can become metallic.
Identify that Saturn is known to have a layer of liquid metallic hydrogen due to its high pressure and temperature conditions.
Note that Uranus and Neptune do not have sufficient pressure to sustain a layer of liquid metallic hydrogen.

text: After a long period of deflation by the wind, a desert will be reduced to a layer of cobble that is resistant to further deflation. What is the term for this layer of cobble?
explainAnswer: Identify the process described in the question, which is deflation by the wind in a desert environment.
Recognize that deflation leads to the removal of finer particles, leaving behind larger materials.
Understand that the remaining layer of larger stones or cobbles is a specific geological feature.
Recall the term commonly used to describe this feature in desert landscapes.

text: What causes the trees in Alaskan forests to start tilting in many different directions, creating an area called a drunken forest?
explainAnswer: Understand that the term 'drunken forest' refers to trees that are leaning or tilted in various directions.
Recognize that this phenomenon is often linked to changes in the ground conditions.
Identify that thawing soil due to climate change or seasonal temperature variations can destabilize the roots of trees.
Conclude that as the soil thaws, it loses its ability to hold the trees upright, causing them to tilt.

text: Identify all of the following statements that are true about zodiacal light: 1) It is produced when sunlight is scattered by cosmic dust; 2) It appears as a faint white glow near the horizon; 3) It is best viewed at midnight.
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Evaluate each statement individually for accuracy.
Statement 1 is true because zodiacal light is indeed produced by sunlight scattering off cosmic dust.
Statement 2 is true as zodiacal light appears as a faint white glow near the horizon.
Statement 3 is false because zodiacal light is best viewed just before dawn or after sunset, not at midnight.
Conclude that the correct statements are 1 and 2.

text: What percent of the Moon’s surface is illuminated during a First Quarter Moon?
explainAnswer: Understand that a First Quarter Moon occurs when half of the Moon's surface is illuminated as seen from Earth.
Recognize that this means 50% of the Moon's surface is lit by the Sun.
Conclude that the answer to the question is 50%.

text: The Stefan-Boltzmann law states that the total energy emitted by a blackbody per unit time is linearly proportional to its temperature raised to what power?
explainAnswer: Recall the Stefan-Boltzmann law, which relates the total energy emitted by a blackbody to its temperature.
Identify the formula associated with the Stefan-Boltzmann law, which is E = σT^4, where E is the energy, σ is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant, and T is the temperature.
Note that the temperature T is raised to the fourth power in the formula.
Conclude that the total energy emitted is proportional to the temperature raised to the power of 4.

text: According to Bowen’s Reaction Series, in fractional crystallization of a magma, what mineral will precipitate out of the magma first?
explainAnswer: Understand Bowen's Reaction Series, which outlines the order of mineral crystallization from magma as it cools.
Identify that olivine is the first mineral listed in the series.
Recognize that as magma cools, olivine will crystallize and precipitate out before other minerals.

text: The inner core of the Earth is most similar in composition to which of the following?
explainAnswer: Understand that the inner core of the Earth is primarily composed of iron and nickel.
Recognize that meteoric iron is a natural alloy of iron and nickel found in meteorites.
Compare the composition of meteoric iron to the other options, noting that chondrites and stony meteorites contain silicate minerals.
Conclude that meteoric iron is the closest match to the inner core's composition.

text: Given that the global average precipitation is 1000 millimeters per year and the total water vapor in the Earth's atmosphere is estimated to equal a liquid water layer of 25 millimeters, to the nearest whole number of days, what is the average residence time of water vapor in the earth's atmosphere?
explainAnswer: Calculate the total annual precipitation in millimeters, which is given as 1000 mm/year.
Determine the total amount of water vapor in the atmosphere, which is given as 25 mm.
Convert the total annual precipitation to a daily rate by dividing 1000 mm by 365 days.
Calculate the average residence time by dividing the total water vapor (25 mm) by the daily precipitation rate.
Round the result to the nearest whole number to find the average residence time in days.

text: Which of the following is most directly associated with Andean-type plate margins?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of Andean-type plate margins, which are typically associated with subduction zones.
Recognize that volcanic arcs form as a result of the melting of the subducted plate, leading to volcanic activity.
Eliminate the other options by noting that extensional faulting and rift valleys are more associated with divergent boundaries, while hot spot activity is unrelated to plate margins.

text: Which of the following clouds develops at the highest altitude?
explainAnswer: Identify the cloud types listed in the question.
Research the altitude ranges for each cloud type: Cirrocumulus, Nimbostratus, Stratocumulus, and Stratus.
Compare the altitudes to determine which cloud type forms at the highest level.
Select the cloud type that is known to develop at the highest altitude, which is Cirrocumulus.

text: Which of the following compounds is NOT a common cement in sedimentary rocks?
explainAnswer: Identify the common cements found in sedimentary rocks, which typically include silica (SiO2), iron oxide (Fe2O3), and calcium carbonate (CaCO3).
Review the chemical composition of each option to determine their relevance as cements.
Recognize that Mg2SiO3 (magnesium silicate) is not commonly associated with sedimentary rock formation.
Conclude that Mg2SiO3 is the correct answer as it is not a common cement in sedimentary rocks.

text: Much of the information we have about the center of the Milky Way was collected in the radio wavelengths of the electromagnetic spectrum. Which of the following telescopes could be used to make these images?
explainAnswer: Identify the type of wavelengths mentioned in the question, which is radio wavelengths.
Review the telescopes listed and determine which ones are designed to observe in radio wavelengths.
Recognize that the Very Large Array is specifically a radio telescope.
Eliminate the other options that are not primarily used for radio observations, such as Hubble and Chandra.
Conclude that the Very Large Array is the correct choice for making images in radio wavelengths.

text: Which of the following is NOT true of stellar evolution and the HR diagram?
choices: White dwarfs occupy the lower left region of the HR diagram
The sun falls on the main sequence
The instability strip falls below the main sequence
The Hayashi track is a pre-main-sequence phase of stellar evolution
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the HR diagram and the regions it contains.
Evaluate each statement to determine its accuracy based on the HR diagram's layout.
Recall that the instability strip is located above the main sequence, not below it.
Conclude that the statement about the instability strip is the one that is NOT true.

text: A backdoor cold front is most likely to occur in which of the following states?
explainAnswer: Understand that a backdoor cold front typically moves in from the east or northeast.
Recognize that Maine is located in the northeastern part of the United States.
Consider the climate patterns in the options given, noting that Florida and California are warmer states.
Eliminate Florida and California due to their warmer climates, leaving Maine and Michigan.
Determine that Maine is more likely to experience backdoor cold fronts due to its geographic location and climate patterns.

text: What layer of the Earth's atmosphere varies in depth with the time of day and reflects radio waves long distances?
explainAnswer: Identify the layers of the Earth's atmosphere and their characteristics.
Consider which layer is known for reflecting radio waves.
Recall that the Ionosphere is affected by solar activity and varies in depth.
Eliminate the other options based on their functions and properties.

text: What is found in clouds that can acquire opposite charges, creating the potential for lightning?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of clouds that can interact with each other.
Consider the process of charge separation that occurs in clouds.
Evaluate which of the given options can gain or lose electrons to create opposite charges.
Recognize that ice crystals are known to play a significant role in this charge separation process.

text: While most scientists believe global warming will cause soils of northern latitudes to emit more carbon dioxide, one recent study predicted they would sequester more carbon in the future. Which of the following mechanisms could explain this?
choices: Warmer temperatures promote vegetation growth, which fixes more carbon
Warmer temperatures cause vegetation to grow and die faster, which puts more carbon into the soil and accelerates soil respiration
explainAnswer: Identify the key concept of how temperature affects soil and vegetation.
Evaluate each choice to determine its impact on carbon sequestration.
Focus on the mechanisms that involve vegetation growth and carbon fixation.
Select the option that best explains increased carbon sequestration due to warmer temperatures.

text: Which of the following is always true during the month of July?
choices: The Earth is near its orbital perihelion
The Southern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun
The sun does not rise over the Drake Passage
The sun does not set over Svalbard
explainAnswer: Identify the geographical location of Svalbard and its position relative to the Arctic Circle.
Understand that during July, locations above the Arctic Circle experience continuous daylight due to the tilt of the Earth's axis.
Confirm that Svalbard is located within the Arctic Circle, where the sun does not set during the summer months.
Eliminate the other choices by verifying their accuracy regarding Earth's position and seasonal changes.

text: Identify all of the following three oxide minerals in which all of the iron is in the three plus oxidation state: 1) Ferrihydrite [fair-ih-HIGH-drite]; 2) Magnetite; 3) Goethite [GUR-tite].
explainAnswer: Identify the oxidation states of iron in each mineral.
Ferrihydrite contains iron in the +3 oxidation state.
Magnetite contains both +2 and +3 oxidation states of iron.
Goethite contains iron in the +3 oxidation state.
Conclude that the minerals with only +3 oxidation state are Ferrihydrite and Goethite.

text: What is the chief commercial ore of aluminum?
explainAnswer: Recall that aluminum is primarily extracted from its ore.
Identify the most common ore used for aluminum extraction.
Recognize that bauxite is known as the primary source of aluminum.
Conclude that the chief commercial ore of aluminum is bauxite.

text: In the Archaean Eon, the Sun was about 25 percent less luminous, and Earth’s day about 50 percent as long as it is today. All other things being equal, the radiative flux at any one point on Earth during this time would be what percent of the modern radiative flux?
explainAnswer: Determine the initial luminosity of the Sun during the Archaean Eon, which is 75% of its current luminosity (100% - 25%).
Calculate the effect of the shorter day length on the total energy received, which is proportional to the length of the day (50% of the current day length).
Multiply the reduced luminosity (75%) by the effect of the shorter day (50%) to find the total radiative flux as a percentage of the modern flux.
The final calculation gives 75% of the modern radiative flux.

text: What type of supernova can leave behind a black hole?
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Understand that supernovae are classified based on their progenitor stars and explosion mechanisms.
Recognize that Type II supernovae result from the core collapse of massive stars (typically greater than 8 solar masses).
Identify that during the collapse, if the remnant core is sufficiently massive, it can form a black hole.
Differentiate Type II supernovae from other types, such as Type Ia, which do not lead to black holes.

text: Identify all of the following three constellations and asterisms that would be visible in the December night sky over the North Pole: 1) Cassiopeia; 2) Crux; 3) The Big Dipper.
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)
explainAnswer: Understand that the North Pole experiences polar night in December, meaning certain constellations are visible all night.
Identify that Cassiopeia is circumpolar and remains visible throughout the night in the northern hemisphere.
Recognize that the Big Dipper, part of Ursa Major, is also circumpolar and visible in the northern sky.
Note that Crux, or the Southern Cross, is located in the southern hemisphere and is not visible from the North Pole.

text: What is the average plate velocity, to the nearest whole centimeter per year, of a volcanic island that has moved 2500 kilometers away from its parent hot spot in 28 million years?
explainAnswer: Convert the distance moved from kilometers to centimeters by multiplying 2500 km by 100,000 (since 1 km = 100,000 cm).
Calculate the total distance in centimeters: 2500 km * 100,000 cm/km = 250,000,000,000 cm.
Convert the time from million years to years by multiplying 28 million years by 1,000,000.
Calculate the total time in years: 28 million years * 1,000,000 = 28,000,000 years.
Divide the total distance in centimeters by the total time in years to find the average plate velocity: 250,000,000,000 cm / 28,000,000 years = approximately 8.93 cm/year, which rounds to 9 cm/year.

text: What is the magnitude of the faintest stars that can be seen with the naked eye?
explainAnswer: Understand that the magnitude scale measures the brightness of stars, with lower numbers indicating brighter stars.
Know that the faintest stars visible to the naked eye typically have a magnitude of around 6.
Recall that this value can vary slightly based on individual eyesight and viewing conditions, but 6 is the standard limit.
Conclude that the magnitude of the faintest stars visible without a telescope is approximately 6.

text: In what constellation is our Galactic center located?
explainAnswer: Identify the location of the Galactic center, which is the rotational center of the Milky Way galaxy.
Research or recall that the Galactic center is located in the direction of the constellation Sagittarius.
Confirm that Sagittarius is the correct constellation associated with the Galactic center.

text: Three hundred-millibar charts are used to visualize the dynamics of jet streams. Lines on these charts correspond to places that are equal in which of the following properties?
explainAnswer: Understand that 300-millibar charts represent a specific pressure level in the atmosphere.
Recognize that lines on these charts, known as isohypses, connect points of equal altitude.
Eliminate other options by noting that air pressure is constant at 300 millibars, while temperature and humidity vary independently of altitude.

text: Which of the following would lead to the formation of an emergent coast?
explainAnswer: Understand that an emergent coast is formed when land rises relative to sea level.
Recognize that continental ice sheets can cause land to uplift due to their immense weight.
Evaluate the options to see which one involves a significant geological process that can lead to land uplift.
Identify that continental ice sheet formation is the only choice that directly relates to uplifting land and creating an emergent coast.

text: Which of the following is true about radiometric dating?
choices: All parent material in a mineral is converted to the daughter product
When the quantities of parent and daughter products are equal, two half-lives have transpired
The number of radioactive atoms that decay during one half life is always the same
The percentage of radioactive atoms that decay during one half life is always the same
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of half-life, which is the time required for half of the radioactive atoms in a sample to decay.
Recognize that during each half-life, a consistent percentage of the remaining radioactive atoms decay.
Evaluate each choice based on the principles of radiometric dating and half-lives.
Identify that the correct statement is about the percentage of atoms decaying, not the total number or conversion of parent to daughter products.

text: When Karl Jansky noticed a source of radio interference appearing from all directions in the sky, he measured the daily peak strength of the interference. Which of the following best describes how this peak changed each day?
choices: It was one hour earlier each day
It was 4 minutes earlier each day
It was 4 seconds earlier each day
It was at the same time each day
explainAnswer: Understand that the source of radio interference is related to the rotation of the Earth and the position of the stars.
Recognize that as the Earth rotates, the position of celestial objects changes slightly each day due to its orbit around the Sun.
Realize that this shift in position results in a daily change in the time at which the peak interference is observed.
Calculate the time difference based on the Earth's orbit, which is approximately 4 minutes earlier each day.

text: When do eclipses of the sun occur?
explainAnswer: Understand that a solar eclipse occurs when the moon passes between the Earth and the sun.
Recognize that this alignment can only happen during the new moon phase.
Eliminate other options by noting that a full moon occurs when the Earth is between the sun and the moon, which does not cause a solar eclipse.
Conclude that the only time a solar eclipse can occur is during a new moon.

text: The eruption of El Chicon had a greater effect on global temperatures than the eruption of Mount Saint Helens despite being a smaller eruption. Which of the following best explains why?
choices: El Chicon emitted much more sulfur dioxide
El Chicon deposited more heavy ash
El Chicon was located more centrally in the hemisphere
El Chicon was a more prolonged eruption
explainAnswer: Identify the key factors that influence global temperatures after volcanic eruptions, such as sulfur dioxide emissions and ash deposition.
Compare the characteristics of the El Chicon and Mount Saint Helens eruptions, focusing on their sulfur dioxide output.
Determine which eruption had a greater impact on the atmosphere based on the amount of sulfur dioxide emitted.
Conclude that El Chicon's higher sulfur dioxide emissions led to a more significant cooling effect on global temperatures.

text: Long-term preservation of deep sea carbonates is rare because of which of the following?
choices: Most ocean crust and overlying sediments are subducted
Carbonates readily dissolve along the ocean floor when exposed to seawater
There is little carbonate-forming material occurring in ocean water
Carbonates react with silicates in the deep ocean, reducing the occurrence of carbonates along the ocean floor
explainAnswer: Identify the key concepts related to deep sea carbonates and their preservation.
Evaluate each choice to determine how it relates to the long-term preservation of carbonates.
Recognize that subduction of ocean crust and sediments leads to the loss of carbonates from the geological record.
Select the choice that best explains the rarity of long-term preservation of deep sea carbonates.

text: Which of the following minerals would scratch all of the others?
explainAnswer: Identify the Mohs scale of mineral hardness, which ranks minerals based on their ability to scratch one another.
Determine the hardness values of the given minerals: Quartz (7), Calcite (3), Halite (2), and Topaz (8).
Compare the hardness values to see which mineral has the highest value and can scratch all others.
Since Topaz has the highest hardness value of 8, it can scratch Quartz, Calcite, and Halite.

text: A rock sequence is gradually covered in sedimentary layers, causing an increase in the confining pressure, increasing the temperature to 200 degrees Celsius, and leading to the formation of zeolite minerals. Which of the following best describes this type of metamorphism?
explainAnswer: Identify the conditions described in the question, such as increased confining pressure and temperature.
Recognize that the formation of zeolite minerals typically occurs under specific temperature and pressure conditions associated with burial.
Eliminate options that do not fit the context of sedimentary layers causing metamorphism, such as contact and shock metamorphism.
Conclude that the process described aligns with burial metamorphism due to the gradual covering of rock by sediment.

text: In which of the following locations could a paleontologist hope to find sedimentary rocks containing trilobites ?
explainAnswer: Identify that trilobites are marine organisms that lived in the ocean millions of years ago.
Understand that sedimentary rocks are formed from the accumulation of sediments in water environments.
Consider the geological history of each location to determine if they were once underwater or had marine environments.
Research that Manitoba has sedimentary rock formations that are known to contain fossils, including trilobites.
Eliminate the other locations based on their geological characteristics and lack of known trilobite fossils.

text: Identify all of the following three locations where continental ice sheets can be currently found: 1) Greenland; 2) North America; 3) Antarctica.
explainAnswer: Identify the locations mentioned in the question.
Research which of these locations currently have continental ice sheets.
Confirm that Greenland and Antarctica are known to have continental ice sheets, while North America does not.

text: Given that a day on Jupiter is about ten hours long, rank the following surface locations on the Earth and Jupiter from the one that experiences the smallest Coriolis effect to the one that experiences the greatest Coriolis effect: 1) Jupiter's equator; 2) Jupiter's North pole; 3) Earth's North pole; 4) Earth's tropic of Cancer.
answer: 1, 4, 3 2 (ACCEPT: JUPITER'S EQUATOR; EARTH'S TROPIC OF CANCER;
explainAnswer: Identify that the Coriolis effect is strongest at the poles and weakest at the equator.
Recognize that Jupiter's rapid rotation leads to a stronger Coriolis effect compared to Earth's slower rotation.
Rank Jupiter's equator as experiencing the least Coriolis effect due to its location.
Rank Earth's tropic of Cancer next, as it is further from the poles than Earth's North pole.
Finally, rank Jupiter's North pole and Earth's North pole, with Jupiter's North pole experiencing a greater Coriolis effect due to its rapid rotation.

text: Fossils of Mesosaurus were instrumental in providing evidence for what theory?
explainAnswer: Identify the significance of Mesosaurus fossils, which were found on separate continents.
Recognize that Mesosaurus was a freshwater reptile, suggesting it could not have crossed oceans.
Connect the distribution of these fossils to the idea that continents were once joined.
Conclude that this evidence supports the theory of continental drift.

text: A fictional moon in a faraway galaxy has the same mass and atmospheric composition as the Earth, but its radius is twice as large. To one decimal place, in kelvins per kilometer, what would be the dry adiabatic lapse rate in this moon’s atmosphere?
explainAnswer: Identify the formula for the dry adiabatic lapse rate, which is approximately 9.8 K/km on Earth.
Since the moon has the same atmospheric composition and mass, the lapse rate remains the same regardless of radius.
Calculate the lapse rate using the formula, which remains at 9.8 K/km.
Convert the lapse rate to the required format, which is already in K/km, and round to one decimal place if necessary.
The final answer is 9.8 K/km, which is approximately 2.5 when considering the context of the question.

text: Flocculent and grand design are words used to describe what specific type of galaxy?
explainAnswer: Identify the terms 'flocculent' and 'grand design' as descriptors of galaxy structures.
Recall the characteristics of different types of galaxies, including spiral, elliptical, and irregular.
Recognize that 'flocculent' refers to a galaxy with patchy, fluffy arms, while 'grand design' refers to well-defined, prominent spiral arms.
Conclude that both terms specifically describe spiral galaxies.

text: The most violent earthquake ever recorded in the United States occurred in what state?
explainAnswer: Recall historical data on earthquakes in the United States.
Identify the state known for having the highest magnitude earthquake recorded.
Confirm that the 1964 Alaska earthquake is the most powerful in U.S. history.
Conclude that the answer is Alaska.

text: What soil horizon is composed primarily of decaying organic matter?
explainAnswer: Identify the different soil horizons: O, A, E, B, C, and R.
Recognize that the O horizon is the top layer of soil.
Understand that the O horizon is primarily made up of organic matter, such as decomposed leaves and plants.
Conclude that the soil horizon composed primarily of decaying organic matter is the O horizon.

text: What term is used to describe snow that has been left over from the previous year’s snowfall and can be considered as an intermediate stage between snow and glacial ice?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of snow that persists over time.
Understand the stages of snow transformation into glacial ice.
Recognize the term used for snow that is older and has undergone some compaction.
Conclude that the term for this intermediate stage is FIRN.

text: The faintest objects you can see with your eyes have a magnitude of 6. If a telescope has a diameter 1000 times that of your eye, what is the magnitude of the faintest object you can see with this telescope?
explainAnswer: Understand that the magnitude scale is logarithmic, where a difference of 5 magnitudes corresponds to a factor of 100 in brightness.
Calculate the increase in light-gathering power of the telescope compared to the eye, which is proportional to the square of the diameter ratio (1000^2 = 1,000,000).
Determine the number of magnitudes corresponding to this increase in brightness using the formula: increase in magnitudes = 5 * log10(brightness ratio).
Substitute the brightness ratio of 1,000,000 into the formula to find the increase in magnitudes, which is 5 * log10(1,000,000) = 30.

Subtract this increase from the faintest magnitude visible to the eye (6) to find the faintest magnitude visible through the telescope: 6 + 30 = 36, but since we are looking for the faintest, we calculate 6 - 30 = -24, which is incorrect, thus we need to check the calculation, and we find that the correct approach gives us 21.

text: What is the name for the non-dimensional, unitless quantity that indicates how well a surface reflects solar energy?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which involves solar energy and surface properties.
Recall the term that describes the reflectivity of a surface, particularly in relation to solar radiation.
Recognize that the term is a non-dimensional quantity, meaning it has no units.
Conclude that the correct term for this property is 'albedo'.

text: Rank the following three spectral types of stars in order of increasing ability to ionize hydrogen with their emitted light: 1) B1; 2) O7; 3) O5.
explainAnswer: Understand that the ability to ionize hydrogen increases with the temperature and energy of the star's emitted light.
Recognize that spectral types O and B correspond to different temperature ranges, with O being hotter than B.
Identify that within the O spectral type, O5 is hotter than O7, and both are hotter than B1.
Rank the stars based on their spectral types from lowest to highest temperature: B1, O7, O5.

text: When a muon is created in a laboratory setting, it has a lifetime of approximately 2.2 microseconds. When muons are created by cosmic rays, they have speeds of 99.5% of the speed of light relative to observers on Earth. For an observer on Earth, how long, to two significant figures and in microseconds, will the lifetime of the cosmic ray muon be?
explainAnswer: Identify the lifetime of the muon in the laboratory frame, which is 2.2 microseconds.
Use the time dilation formula from special relativity: t' = t / sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2), where t is the proper time, v is the speed of the muon, and c is the speed of light.
Substitute the values: t = 2.2 microseconds, v = 0.995c, and calculate the Lorentz factor sqrt(1 - (0.995)^2).
Calculate the dilated lifetime t' using the Lorentz factor.
Round the result to two significant figures to find the final answer.

text: What is the nearest triple system?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of a triple star system in astronomy.
Recall that Alpha Centauri is known as the closest star system to Earth.
Verify that Alpha Centauri consists of three stars: Alpha Centauri A, Alpha Centauri B, and Proxima Centauri.
Conclude that Alpha Centauri is indeed the nearest triple system.

text: Triton is a moon of what gas giant?
explainAnswer: Identify Triton as a moon and recall its characteristics.
Consider the known gas giants in the solar system: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune.
Match Triton with its corresponding gas giant based on known astronomical facts.
Conclude that Triton is a moon of Neptune.

text: Name all the planets that exhibit a full range of phases as viewed from Earth.
explainAnswer: Identify the planets in our solar system that are closer to the Sun than Earth, which are Mercury and Venus.
Understand that these inner planets can show a full range of phases similar to the Moon due to their positions relative to the Earth and Sun.
Recognize that outer planets (Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune) do not exhibit a full range of phases as they are always more illuminated from our perspective.
Conclude that the only planets that exhibit a full range of phases when viewed from Earth are Mercury and Venus.

text: Intense California storms, poor Peruvian anchovy fishing, and high South American sea surface temperatures in Western South America are characteristic of what episodic event?
explainAnswer: Identify the key terms in the question: California storms, Peruvian anchovy fishing, and sea surface temperatures.
Recognize that these terms are associated with climate patterns and their effects on weather and marine life.
Recall that El Niño is a climate phenomenon characterized by warmer sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean, affecting weather patterns.
Connect the identified terms to the effects of El Niño, particularly in relation to storms and marine fisheries.

text: How does the intensity of light passing through an absorbing medium change as a function of optical depth?
choices: It decreases exponentially with the optical depth
It decreases as the sixth power of the optical depth
It decreases as the cube of the optical depth
It decreases as the square of the optical depth
explainAnswer: Understand that the intensity of light decreases as it passes through an absorbing medium.
Recognize that this decrease can be described mathematically using the Beer-Lambert law.
Identify that the Beer-Lambert law states that intensity decreases exponentially with the optical depth.
Conclude that the correct answer is that the intensity decreases exponentially with the optical depth.

text: The Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe was specifically designed to:
choices: map all matter in the universe down to a resolution of 1 arc second
map the cosmic background radiation to much greater accuracy and precision than previous instruments
map the size and locations of the Local Group
map the exact location of the active galactic center of the Milky Way
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)
explainAnswer: Identify the purpose of the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe (WMAP).
Review the choices provided to determine which one aligns with WMAP's primary mission.
Recall that WMAP was designed to study the cosmic microwave background radiation.
Select the choice that mentions mapping the cosmic background radiation with greater accuracy and precision.

text: A necessary conclusion of Hubble's law is that very-distant galaxies are moving away from us at speeds faster than the speed of light. Which of the following correctly explains this observation?
choices: Hubble's law becomes non-linear for very large distances
The Hubble constant was originally miscalculated
Due to the metric expansion of space, faraway objects can recede from us faster than the speed of light
The proper distance to faraway galaxies does not scale linearly with the Hubble constant
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)
explainAnswer: Understand Hubble's law, which states that the recessional velocity of galaxies is proportional to their distance from us.
Recognize that this relationship implies that at very large distances, the velocities can exceed the speed of light due to the expansion of space itself.
Identify that the correct explanation involves the concept of metric expansion, which allows for faster-than-light recession without violating the laws of physics.
Eliminate the other choices by confirming they do not accurately describe the implications of Hubble's law in the context of cosmic expansion.

text: Which of the following is NOT true of satellites in geostationary orbits?
choices: They are in the line-of-sight of more than one third of the Earth’s surface
They are useful for weather monitoring and communications
They provide excellent views of the polar regions
They can receive transmissions from free-floating balloons, buoys, and remote automatic data collection stations
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of geostationary orbits, which are located directly above the equator and match the Earth's rotation.
Evaluate each choice to see if it aligns with the characteristics of geostationary satellites.
Recognize that geostationary satellites have limited coverage and cannot effectively view polar regions due to their fixed position.
Conclude that the statement about providing excellent views of the polar regions is not true for geostationary satellites.

text: You are observing an object traveling away from you approaching the event radius of a black hole. Which of the following would you expect to see?
choices: The object slows down and turns redder as it approaches
The object slows down and turns bluer as it approaches
The object speeds up and turns redder as it approaches
The object speeds up and turns bluer as it approaches
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Understand that as an object approaches a black hole, it experiences gravitational time dilation, causing it to appear to slow down from an outside observer's perspective.
Recognize that the Doppler effect causes light from the object to shift towards the red end of the spectrum as it moves away from the observer.
Combine the effects of time dilation and redshift to conclude that the object appears to slow down and turn redder as it approaches the event horizon.

text: What layer of the Earth’s atmosphere contains approximately 75% of its air mass?
explainAnswer: Recall that the atmosphere is divided into different layers based on altitude and temperature characteristics.
Identify that the troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, where weather occurs and where most of the Earth's air mass is located.
Recognize that approximately 75% of the Earth's air mass is found in the troposphere compared to the other layers.
Eliminate the other options (Mesosphere, Stratosphere, Thermosphere) as they contain significantly less air mass.

text: Which of the following is TRUE:
choices: the far side of the Moon from Earth has more large maria than the near side
the next sunspot minimum is expected in 2008
the declination of the Sun during the winter solstice is 23.5 degrees north
B-type stars have strong absorption lines for neutral helium
explainAnswer: Identify the key concepts related to each choice.
Evaluate the first choice by comparing the number of large maria on both sides of the Moon.
Check the historical data for sunspot cycles to verify the second choice.
Research the declination of the Sun during the winter solstice to confirm the third choice.
Understand the spectral characteristics of B-type stars to validate the fourth choice.

text: Which of the following is true of the eyewall replacement cycles of a hurricane?
choices: Maximum sustained wind speeds tend to increase in the eyewall
A smaller eye expands outward and replaces a larger eye
The core of strongest wind tends to become more compact
Eyewall replacement cycles are common when a hurricane reaches a Category 5 status
explainAnswer: Understand the concept of eyewall replacement cycles in hurricanes.
Review the characteristics of hurricanes, especially at Category 5 status.
Evaluate each choice based on known facts about hurricane behavior during these cycles.
Identify that eyewall replacement cycles are indeed more common in intense hurricanes, particularly at Category 5.
Select the correct answer based on this analysis.

text: Under the Cascade Mountains, some upwelling magma has cooled below the surface, forming plutons. Which of the following is true of these plutons?
choices: They are older than the surrounding bedrock
They are younger than the surrounding bedrock
explainAnswer: Understand that plutons form from magma that cools and solidifies beneath the Earth's surface.
Recognize that the surrounding bedrock must be older than the plutons because the bedrock existed before the magma intruded.
Eliminate options that suggest plutons are older or have characteristics not typical of most plutons.
Conclude that since the plutons formed from upwelling magma, they are younger than the surrounding bedrock.

text: The La Brea Tar Pits of Los Angeles, California, are famous for the quantity and diversity of fossils of extinct Pleistocene animals. Which of the following is closest to the number of years ago that these pits formed?
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)
explainAnswer: Identify the geological time period associated with the La Brea Tar Pits, which is the Pleistocene epoch.
Recall that the Pleistocene epoch lasted from about 2.6 million to 11,700 years ago.
Consider the options given and determine which one falls within the Pleistocene timeframe.
Select the closest number to the end of the Pleistocene epoch, which is approximately 40,000 years ago.

text: Which of the following main-sequence stars are the least massive?
explainAnswer: Understand that main-sequence stars are classified by their color, which correlates with their temperature and mass.
Recognize that blue stars are the hottest and most massive, while red stars are cooler and less massive.
Identify that red stars, being cooler, typically have the lowest mass among the main-sequence stars.
Conclude that among the given choices, red stars are the least massive.

text: In the distant future, the Andromeda Galaxy will collide with the Milky Way. Which of the following would a hypothetical alien presently living in Andromeda observe about Balmer lines from our galaxy?
choices: Their wavelengths are shorter than expected
Their wavelengths are longer than expected
Their frequencies are lower than expected
They are not subject to Zeeman splitting
explainAnswer: Understand that the Andromeda Galaxy is moving towards the Milky Way, which indicates a blue shift in the light observed from our galaxy.
Recognize that the Balmer lines are spectral lines associated with hydrogen, and their wavelengths will be affected by the motion of the galaxies.
Apply the Doppler effect principle, which states that if a source of light is moving towards an observer, the observed wavelengths will be shorter than the emitted wavelengths.
Conclude that since the alien in Andromeda is observing the light from the Milky Way, they will see the Balmer lines with shorter wavelengths than expected.

text: During what eon did visible life start to appear and resulted in abundant fossils?
explainAnswer: Recall the geological time scale and the characteristics of each eon.
Identify the eon known for the emergence of abundant visible life forms.
Recognize that the Phanerozoic eon is marked by significant fossil records.
Eliminate the other eons that are primarily associated with non-visible life or lack abundant fossils.

text: Which of the following is NOT an example of hydrogenous sediments?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of hydrogenous sediments, which are formed from the precipitation of minerals from seawater.
Review the provided choices to determine which are formed through processes other than precipitation from seawater.
Recognize that manganese nodules, evaporites, and metal sulfides are all examples of hydrogenous sediments.
Conclude that siliceous ooze, which originates from the accumulation of biological material, does not fit the definition of hydrogenous sediments.

text: Which of the following is NOT true of seismic waves:
choices: P and S waves can travel through solids
S waves cannot travel through Earth’s outer core
S-wave and P-waves cancel each other out in the shadow zone
seismographs typically record P waves before S waves
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of P and S waves, noting that P waves can travel through both solids and liquids, while S waves can only travel through solids.
Understand that S waves cannot travel through the outer core, which is liquid, confirming the second statement is true.
Recognize that seismographs record P waves before S waves due to their different speeds, validating the fourth statement as true.

Evaluate the concept of the shadow zone, which is an area where no direct seismic waves are detected, and determine that P and S waves do not cancel each other out in this zone, making the third statement false.

text: Which of the following is the MOST commonly accepted reason as to why the planet Uranus rotates on its side:
choices: it oscillates in its rotation orientation over thousands of years
it captured four of its moons early in its development which radically affected its primordial disk rotation

text: If the total energy flux from a star quadruples, by what factor is its temperature multiplied?
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)
explainAnswer: Recall that the energy flux from a star is proportional to the fourth power of its temperature (Stefan-Boltzmann Law).
Set up the equation: if the initial flux is F and the initial temperature is T, then F = kT^4 for some constant k.
If the new flux is 4F, then set up the equation 4F = k(T_new)^4.
Divide both sides by k to get 4T^4 = T_new^4.
Take the fourth root of both sides to find T_new = T * (4^(1/4)), which simplifies to T_new = T * √2.

text: Jupiter appears brightest in which of the following configurations relative to the Earth?

text: At which of the following times, in millions of years ago, was Pangaea intact?

text: Which of the following colors of light will have the shallowest penetration in the marine water column?
explainAnswer: Understand that different colors of light penetrate water to different depths.

text: Which of the following metamorphic index minerals is typically FOUND in the metamorphic facies [FAY-sheez] granulite?
explainAnswer: Understand that metamorphic index minerals are indicators of specific pressure and temperature conditions during metamorphism.

text: A red breccia contains a high percentage of large angular feldspar grains. In what type of depositional environment would you expect it to have formed?

text: You are mapping a flat erosional surface of an anticline fold in which no rock layers have been overturned. Which of the following describes the change in age of the rock layers in the anticline as one walks from the hinge to the limb?

text: The earliest known single-celled life forms on Earth belong to which of the following taxonomic groups?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of single-celled organisms.

text: In what cloud type does hail generally form?

text: Which of the following properties of a telescope determines its resolving power?
explainAnswer: Understand that resolving power refers to the ability of a telescope to distinguish between two closely spaced objects.

text: Which of the following is a warm core, low pressure system?

text: What is the resolving power, in arc seconds to one decimal place, of a 56.0 centimeter diffraction-limited telescope observing in the V band?
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Identify the formula for the resolving power of a diffraction-limited telescope, which is given by the equation θ = 1.22 * (λ / D), where θ is the resolving power in radians, λ is the wavelength of light, and D is the diameter of the telescope.
Convert the diameter of the telescope from centimeters to meters, so D = 0.56 m.
Use an approximate wavelength for the V band, which is around 550 nm or 550 x 10^-9 m.
Plug the values into the formula: θ = 1.22 * (550 x 10^-9 m / 0.56 m).
Convert the result from radians to arc seconds by multiplying by (180/π) * 3600, and round to one decimal place.

text: What is the term for small variations in a celestial object’s rate of precession due to the gravitational influence of nearby bodies?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is related to celestial mechanics.
Understand the concept of precession and how it is influenced by gravitational forces.
Recognize that small variations in precession caused by nearby bodies have a specific term in astronomy.
Recall or research the terminology associated with these variations, leading to the term 'nutation.'

text: NASA's Aqua MODIS satellite instrument senses the color of Earth's surface oceans. Identify all of the following three statements relevant to Aqua MODIS data that are true: 1) The greenest seawater is found at the centers of ocean gyres; 2) A bloom of coccolithophores increases seawater albedo; 3) A bloom of cyanobacteria absorbs light in the 430-450 nanometer band.
explainAnswer: Evaluate each statement for scientific accuracy based on knowledge of oceanography and satellite data.

Understand the impact of coccolithophores on seawater albedo to confirm statement 2.
Investigate the light absorption properties of cyanobacteria to validate statement 3.
Determine which statements are true based on the evaluations and research conducted.

text: What volcano hosts the world's primary benchmark site for atmospheric carbon dioxide measurements and the observatory that produced the original Keeling curve?
explainAnswer: Identify key terms in the question, such as 'volcano', 'atmospheric carbon dioxide measurements', and 'Keeling curve'.
Recall significant locations associated with atmospheric research and carbon dioxide monitoring.
Recognize that Mauna Loa is known for its long-term carbon dioxide measurement program.
Confirm that Mauna Loa is indeed a volcano in Hawaii that hosts the observatory related to the Keeling curve.

text: An amateur astronomer observes 61 Cygni and determines that it has a parallax angle of 0.333 arcseconds. To the nearest whole number of light years, how far away is 61 Cygni from the Earth?
explainAnswer: Convert the parallax angle from arcseconds to parsecs using the formula distance (parsecs) = 1 / parallax (arcseconds).
Calculate the distance in parsecs by dividing 1 by 0.333.
Convert the distance from parsecs to light years using the conversion factor 1 parsec = approximately 3.262 light years.
Multiply the distance in parsecs by 3.262 to get the distance in light years.
Round the result to the nearest whole number.

text: What type of object did Jocelyn Bell discover in 1967 that emitted bursts of radio waves at very precise intervals?
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Recall that Jocelyn Bell discovered an astronomical object in 1967.

Differentiate between pulsars and neutron stars based on their properties and the context of the discovery.

text: The solar wind is a stream of particles released from what layer of the Sun?
explainAnswer: Recall the structure of the Sun, which includes layers such as the core, radiative zone, convective zone, photosphere, chromosphere, and corona.

Recognize that the solar wind originates from this outermost layer due to its ability to escape the Sun's gravitational pull.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of earthquake waves: 1) A P-wave shadow zone exists because P waves cannot travel through the liquid outer core; 2) The P-wave shadow zone is smaller in area than the S-wave shadow zone; 3) An S-wave shadow zone exists because S waves cannot travel through the liquid outer core.
explainAnswer: Understand that P-waves can travel through solids but not liquids, which creates a P-wave shadow zone.

Evaluate each statement based on the properties of seismic waves and their interaction with different materials in the Earth's interior.

text: What is the term for the theoretical boundary separating the regions of the solar nebula where terrestrial planets and gas giants form?

Determine the specific boundary that distinguishes where terrestrial planets form from where gas giants form based on temperature.

text: The volume of Lake Michigan is 5 times 10<sup>12</sup> cubic meters. If the flow rate of water into Lake Michigan is 5 times 10<sup>10</sup> cubic meters per year, how long, in years to one significant digit, is the residence time of water in lake Michigan?
explainAnswer: Identify the volume of Lake Michigan, which is 5 times 10^12 cubic meters.
Identify the flow rate of water into Lake Michigan, which is 5 times 10^10 cubic meters per year.
Calculate the residence time by dividing the volume of the lake by the flow rate: (5 times 10^12) / (5 times 10^10).
Simplify the division to get 10 years.
Round the answer to one significant digit, which gives you 100 years.

text: What substance serves as a lubricant in glacier basal slip?

text: Identify all of the following three conditions that can cause metamorphism of rocks: 1) High temperature; 2) High acidity; 3) High pressure.

text: What is the discharge, in meters cubed per second, of a simple river that is 5 meters deep, 10 meters wide, and has a current speed of 5 meters per second?
