text: The Oso landslide that occurred in Washington State in 2014 moved 1.2 kilometers across the North Fork Stillaguamish River in a single minute. What was the speed of this landslide in miles per hour, rounded to the nearest tenth?
explainAnswer: Convert the distance from kilometers to miles by using the conversion factor 1 kilometer = 0.621371 miles.
Calculate the distance in miles: 1.2 kilometers * 0.621371 = 0.746 miles.
Since the landslide moved this distance in one minute, convert the time from minutes to hours by multiplying by 60.
Calculate the speed in miles per hour: speed = distance in miles / time in hours = 0.746 miles / (1/60) hours = 44.76 miles per hour.
Round the speed to the nearest tenth to get 44.7 miles per hour.

text: Identify all of the following four rocks that would be classified as foliated metamorphic rocks: 1) Gneiss; 2) Marble; 3) Quartzite; 4) Phyllite.

text: Christmas Pie is a small hamlet in Surrey, England, at 51.25 degrees north latitude. In degrees to the nearest integer, what is the noon sun angle over Christmas Pie on the winter solstice?

Calculate the noon sun angle using the formula: noon sun angle = 90 degrees - (latitude + declination).
Substitute the values: noon sun angle = 90 - (51.25 - 23.5).
Simplify the calculation to find the noon sun angle, rounding to the nearest integer.

text: What is the period in years of two stars, each with a mass of two solar masses, in an orbit with a semi-major axis of 1600 AU and an eccentricity of 0.5?
explainAnswer: Use Kepler's Third Law, which states that the square of the period of orbit (P) is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis (a) of the orbit, adjusted for the total mass of the system.
Calculate the total mass of the two stars, which is 2 solar masses + 2 solar masses = 4 solar masses.
Convert the semi-major axis from AU to meters, knowing that 1 AU = 1.496 x 10^11 meters, so 1600 AU = 2.394 x 10^14 meters.
Apply Kepler's Third Law: P^2 = (4π^2 / G(M1 + M2)) * a^3, where G is the gravitational constant, M1 and M2 are the masses of the stars, and a is the semi-major axis in meters.
Solve for P and convert the result from seconds to years to find the period in years, which yields approximately 32000 years.

text: Identify all of the following three moraine types that form perpendicular to the direction of glacial flow: 1) Lateral moraine [mah-RAYN]; 2) End moraine; 3) Medial moraine.

text: What element is responsible for the destructive nature of CFCs to ozone molecules?

text: Neptune appears a shade of blue because of what atmospheric gas mixed in with hydrogen and helium?

text: What term describes the change of direction in a wave as it enters shallower water?

text: What is the name for a cloud that looks like a pouch and often forms hanging down from the underside of the anvil of a cumulonimbus cloud?

text: Identify all of the following three mineral properties that can be used to distinguish gold from pyrite: 1) Streak; 2) Density; 3) Mohs hardness.

text: The approximate surface temperature of our Sun is 5800 kelvins, while the approximate surface temperature of the blue giant star Rigel is 11,600 kelvins. explainAnswer: Identify the Stefan-Boltzmann law, which states that the power radiated per unit area of a black body is proportional to the fourth power of its temperature (P ∝ T^4).

Raise this ratio to the fourth power to find the ratio of the radiative power per unit area: (T_Rigel / T_Sun)^4.
Substitute the values: (11600 / 5800)^4 = (2)^4 = 16.
Conclude that Rigel generates 16 times as much radiative power per unit of surface area as the Sun.

Recognize that carbon dioxide is known for its significant role in enhancing the greenhouse effect due to its ability to absorb infrared radiation.
Conclude that the primary gas responsible for the greenhouse effect on Venus is carbon dioxide.

text: In what phase is the Moon when moonrise occurs at noon?
explainAnswer: Understand that moonrise occurs when the Moon is on the eastern horizon.
Determine that noon corresponds to the Sun being at its highest point in the sky.
Recognize that during the First Quarter phase, the Moon is 90 degrees ahead of the Sun in the sky.
Conclude that if the Sun is at its highest point at noon, the First Quarter Moon will be rising in the east.

text: What element is the net product formed by the CNO cycle that takes place in hot stars?
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Understand that the CNO cycle is a series of nuclear fusion reactions that convert hydrogen into helium in stars.
Recognize that the primary output of these reactions is helium, as hydrogen nuclei (protons) fuse together.
Identify that the CNO cycle involves carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen as catalysts, but the end product is helium.
Conclude that the net product formed by the CNO cycle is helium.

text: What is the nearest galaxy cluster?
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of galaxy clusters and their significance in astronomy.
Research the nearest galaxy clusters to Earth using astronomical databases or resources.
Determine the distance of the Virgo cluster in relation to other known clusters.
Confirm that the Virgo cluster is recognized as the closest galaxy cluster to the Milky Way.

text: Identify all of the following three latitudes that trade winds can be found in: 1) Between 60 and 30 degrees south; 2) Between 30 degrees south and the equator; 3) Between the equator and 30 degrees north.
explainAnswer: Understand that trade winds are primarily found in the tropics, which are between the equator and 30 degrees north and south.
Identify that the latitudes between 60 and 30 degrees south are outside the tropical region, where trade winds do not occur.
Recognize that the region between 30 degrees south and the equator is one of the areas where trade winds blow from the east.
Note that the region between the equator and 30 degrees north also experiences trade winds, as they are part of the same tropical belt.

text: The galactic center of the Milky Way is in what constellation?
explainAnswer: Identify that the question is asking for a specific constellation.
Recall that the Milky Way galaxy has a central region known as the galactic center.
Know that the galactic center is located in the direction of the constellation Sagittarius.
Conclude that the correct answer is Sagittarius.

text: What type of tide has a single high and a single low during a 24-hour period?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of tides: diurnal, semidiurnal, and mixed.
Understand that diurnal tides have one high tide and one low tide each lunar day.
Recognize that semidiurnal tides have two high tides and two low tides in the same period.
Conclude that the type of tide with a single high and a single low during a 24-hour period is diurnal.

text: Identify all of the following three actions that would decrease the temperature at which a subducting rock becomes a magma: 1) Increase pressure; 2) Increase water content; 3) Increase silica content.
explainAnswer: Understand that increasing pressure generally raises the melting temperature of rocks.
Recognize that adding water lowers the melting temperature of rocks due to the formation of hydrous minerals.
Identify that increasing silica content can also lower the melting temperature by creating more felsic compositions.

text: What river has the largest drainage basin in the United States?
explainAnswer: Identify the major rivers in the United States.
Research the drainage basins associated with these rivers.
Compare the sizes of the drainage basins to determine which is the largest.
Confirm that the Mississippi River has the largest drainage basin in the United States.

text: Identify all of the following three events that occurred during the recombination epoch of the Big Bang: 1) Formation of neutral hydrogen; 2) Neutrino decoupling; 3) Star formation.
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)
explainAnswer: Understand the timeline of the Big Bang and identify the recombination epoch as the period when the universe cooled enough for protons and electrons to combine into neutral hydrogen.
Recognize that neutrino decoupling occurred earlier, about one second after the Big Bang, not during the recombination epoch.
Note that star formation happened much later, after the recombination epoch, during the era of structure formation.
Conclude that only the formation of neutral hydrogen occurred during the recombination epoch.

text: What is the term for the vertical motions that occur when the atmosphere is unstable?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which involves atmospheric science.
Recall the concepts related to vertical motions in the atmosphere.
Understand that unstable atmospheric conditions lead to rising and falling air.
Recognize that the process responsible for these vertical motions is called convection.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of the inner planets: 1) Mercury has an atmosphere of primarily methane; 2) All of the inner planets revolve in the same direction around the sun; 3) All of the inner planets rotate in the same direction around their axes.
explainAnswer: Evaluate each statement for accuracy based on known facts about the inner planets.
Identify that Mercury does not have a significant atmosphere, let alone one primarily composed of methane, making statement 1 false.
Confirm that all inner planets (Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars) revolve around the sun in the same direction (counterclockwise), validating statement 2 as true.
Check the rotation direction of the inner planets; while most rotate counterclockwise, Venus rotates clockwise, making statement 3 false.
Conclude that only statement 2 is true.

text: Identify all of the following three features that are associated with karst landscapes. 1) Disappearing streams; 2) Stalagmites [stah-LAG-mites]; 3) Sinkholes.
explainAnswer: Understand that karst landscapes are formed by the dissolution of soluble rocks such as limestone.
Recognize that disappearing streams are a common feature in karst regions where water flows into underground channels.
Identify that stalagmites form in caves, which are prevalent in karst landscapes due to the presence of limestone.
Acknowledge that sinkholes are depressions or holes that occur when the ground collapses, often found in karst areas.
Conclude that all three features are indeed associated with karst landscapes.

text: What acid, formed from the reaction of carbon dioxide and water, is the most common agent of chemical weathering on Earth’s surface?
explainAnswer: Identify the reactants involved in the reaction, which are carbon dioxide (CO2) and water (H2O).
Recognize that when CO2 dissolves in water, it forms carbonic acid (H2CO3).
Understand that carbonic acid is a weak acid that contributes to the weathering of rocks and minerals.
Conclude that the most common agent of chemical weathering on Earth’s surface is carbonic acid.

text: How many times greater, in terms of energy, is a magnitude 6 earthquake than a magnitude 4 earthquake?
explainAnswer: Understand that the Richter scale is logarithmic, meaning each whole number increase on the scale represents a tenfold increase in measured amplitude and approximately 31.6 times more energy release.
Calculate the difference in magnitude between the two earthquakes: 6 - 4 = 2.
Raise 31.6 to the power of the difference in magnitude: 31.6^2.
Calculate 31.6^2 to find the energy difference: 31.6 * 31.6 = 998.56.
Round the result to the nearest whole number, which is approximately 961.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of the Eagle Nebula: 1) It is an emission nebula; 2) It has a diameter of about 1 million light years; 3) It is part of the Kuiper belt.
explainAnswer: Evaluate each statement individually for accuracy.
Research the classification of the Eagle Nebula to confirm it is an emission nebula.
Check the diameter of the Eagle Nebula and compare it to the stated 1 million light years.
Investigate the location of the Eagle Nebula to see if it is part of the Kuiper belt.

text: Phosphorus is an essential nutrient for phytoplankton. Identify all of the following three processes that remove phosphorus from the Indian Ocean photic zone: 1) Marine snow; 2) Coastal upwelling; 3) Deposition of windblown dust from Australia.
explainAnswer: Understand that marine snow refers to organic and inorganic particles that fall from the upper layers of the ocean to the deeper layers, effectively removing phosphorus from the photic zone.
Recognize that coastal upwelling brings nutrient-rich water from the deep ocean to the surface, which does not remove phosphorus but rather supplies it.
Acknowledge that deposition of windblown dust from Australia may introduce nutrients, including phosphorus, into the ocean rather than removing it.
Conclude that only marine snow is a process that removes phosphorus from the Indian Ocean photic zone.

text: A star has five times the radius of the Sun, and the temperature in kelvins of its surface is twice that of the Sun. How many times as luminous as the Sun is it?
explainAnswer: Use the formula for luminosity: L = 4πR^2σT^4, where R is the radius, T is the temperature, and σ is the Stefan-Boltzmann constant.
Substitute the radius of the star (5 times the Sun's radius) into the formula: R_star = 5R_sun.
Substitute the temperature of the star (2 times the Sun's temperature) into the formula: T_star = 2T_sun.
Calculate the luminosity of the star: L_star = 4π(5R_sun)^2σ(2T_sun)^4.
Simplify the expression to find L_star in terms of L_sun, which results in L_star = 400L_sun.

text: Place the following three events in Earth history in chronological order: 1) Core separation; 2) Moon-forming impact; 3) Formation of atmosphere.
explainAnswer: Identify the events and their significance in Earth's history.
Determine the sequence of events based on geological and astronomical evidence.
Recognize that core separation occurred first as the planet differentiated.
Understand that the Moon-forming impact happened after core separation as a result of a collision with a Mars-sized body.
Conclude that the formation of the atmosphere occurred last as volcanic activity and other processes released gases.

text: What is the right ascension, to the nearest hour, of the Sun on the summer solstice?
explainAnswer: Understand that the summer solstice occurs around June 21st in the Northern Hemisphere.
Know that the Sun's position in the sky is measured in right ascension, which is similar to longitude but for celestial objects.
Recognize that during the summer solstice, the Sun is at its highest point in the sky at noon and is located at approximately 90 degrees from the vernal equinox point.
Convert this position into right ascension, which is measured in hours, with 24 hours corresponding to 360 degrees.
Calculate that 90 degrees corresponds to 6 hours of right ascension.

text: Land that has been frozen for at least two years, including rock or soil, has what classification?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of land that has been frozen for at least two years.
Consider the characteristics of frozen land, including rock or soil.
Recall the specific term used to describe this type of land.
Conclude that the classification for this land is PERMAFROST.

text: According to the Stefan-Boltzmann law, a star with surface temperature in kelvins that is three times that of the Sun would emit how many times as much energy as the Sun?
explainAnswer: Identify the Stefan-Boltzmann law, which states that the power emitted per unit area of a black body is proportional to the fourth power of its temperature (P ∝ T^4).
Let the surface temperature of the Sun be T, then the temperature of the star is 3T.
Substitute the star's temperature into the Stefan-Boltzmann law: P_star ∝ (3T)^4.
Calculate (3T)^4, which equals 81T^4.
Since P_sun ∝ T^4, the ratio of the power emitted by the star to that of the Sun is 81, meaning the star emits 81 times as much energy as the Sun.

text: What term is given to the layer of an ocean or lake that extends from the surface to the depth at which 99 percent of the surface light has been absorbed?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which relates to aquatic ecosystems.
Understand the concept of light penetration in water bodies.
Recognize that the layer where most light is available is crucial for photosynthesis.
Recall the specific term used to describe this light-penetrated layer.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true regarding winds: 1) In general, winds at the equator flow west; 2) Air rising from the equator sinks around 5 degrees north and south latitudes; 3) At 30 degrees south latitude, the sinking air generally yields clear skies.
explainAnswer: Evaluate the first statement about equatorial winds and determine if they generally flow west.
Assess the second statement regarding air rising from the equator and whether it sinks at 5 degrees north and south latitudes.
Analyze the third statement about sinking air at 30 degrees south latitude and its effect on sky conditions.
Identify which statements are true based on your evaluations and select the correct ones.

text: Two stars have the same absolute magnitude. One is at a distance of 10 parsecs and the other is at a distance of 100 parsecs. What is the positive difference in their apparent magnitudes?
explainAnswer: Recall that the difference in apparent magnitude between two stars can be calculated using the distance modulus formula: m - M = 5 log10(d) - 5.
Since both stars have the same absolute magnitude (M), the difference in their apparent magnitudes (m1 - m2) will depend only on their distances.
Calculate the apparent magnitude for the star at 10 parsecs: m1 = M + 5 log10(10) - 5 = M + 0.
Calculate the apparent magnitude for the star at 100 parsecs: m2 = M + 5 log10(100) - 5 = M + 10.
Find the positive difference: |m1 - m2| = |(M + 0) - (M + 10)| = 10 - 0 = 10, but since we are looking for the difference in distance, we use the fact that the difference in magnitudes is 5.

text: On what tectonic plate does most of the North American continent rest?
explainAnswer: Identify the major tectonic plates that encompass the North American continent.
Determine which plate is primarily associated with the landmass of North America.
Confirm that the North American Plate is the correct designation for this tectonic plate.
Conclude that the majority of the North American continent rests on the North American Plate.

text: Identify all of the following three characteristics that can be used to distinguish the mineral calcite from the mineral quartz: 1) Color; 2) Hardness; 3) Birefringence [bye-ree-FRIN-jents].
explainAnswer: Understand that hardness is a key characteristic, with calcite being softer (3 on Mohs scale) compared to quartz (7 on Mohs scale).
Recognize that birefringence is a property of calcite, which exhibits double refraction, while quartz does not.
Note that color is not a reliable distinguishing characteristic since both minerals can appear in various colors.

text: What is the name for the air-lifting process that forces an air mass up and over a mountain or upland, causing the moisture to rain out on the windward slope and leaving a rainshadow effect on the leeward slope?
explainAnswer: Identify the process related to air movement and mountains.
Recall the term used to describe the lifting of air over a topographical barrier.
Consider the effects of this process on precipitation patterns.
Conclude with the specific term that describes this phenomenon.

text: Put the following four minerals in order from softest to hardest on the Mohs scale: 1) Apatite; 2) Fluorite; 3) Quartz; 4) Corundum.
explainAnswer: Identify the Mohs hardness values for each mineral: Apatite (5), Fluorite (4), Quartz (7), Corundum (9).
List the minerals along with their hardness values.
Arrange the minerals in ascending order based on their hardness values.
Confirm the order: Fluorite (4), Apatite (5), Quartz (7), Corundum (9).
Present the final order as 2, 1, 3, 4.

text: Wa t e r-saturated surfaces can behave like liquids during earthquakes. What is the term for this phenomenon?

text: Into what units of geologic time are periods divided?

text: Why does dolostone weather to a brownish colored rock?

Aluminum ions replace the calcium in the dolomite compounds, and there is a reaction between aluminum and the remaining magnesium ions
Magnesium ions replace the calcium ions in dolostone compounds

Understand the role of iron in the weathering process of dolostone.
Evaluate how the replacement of magnesium by iron affects the color of the rock.
Consider the other options and eliminate them based on their relevance to the color change.

text: Order the following three cloud types in increasing order of elevation in the Earth’s atmosphere: 1) Altocumulus; 2) Cirrocumulus; 3) Stratocumulus.
explainAnswer: Identify the elevation ranges for each cloud type: Stratocumulus (low), Altocumulus (mid), and Cirrocumulus (high).

Assign the corresponding numbers to each cloud type based on their elevation order.

text: What rock is transitional between igneous and metamorphic rocks, in which the felsic minerals have melted and recrystalized but the mafic [MAA-fik] minerals have not?
explainAnswer: Understand the definitions of igneous and metamorphic rocks.
Identify the characteristics of a rock that is transitional between these two types.
Recognize that migmatite is formed when felsic minerals melt and recrystallize while mafic minerals remain unchanged.

text: The Black Hills of South Dakota is a large dome that has been exposed due to upwarping followed by erosion. Which of the following rocks would we expect to find in the innermost core of the Black Hills?

text: What is the dominant gas of the Martian atmosphere?

Identify the primary gases found in the Martian atmosphere.

text: Which of these is true regarding the Sargasso sea?

It is adjacent to the Bay of Bengal

It has the saltiest ocean water

text: A poikiloblastic [poi-kil-uh-BLAS-tik] texture is characterized by which of the following?

Homogeneously [hoh-muh-JEE-nee-uhs-li] xenoblastic with little to no evidence of additional alteration minerals

text: Which of the following is NOT true:
choices: an eclipse of the Moon only occurs during a full Moon

an event horizon is associated with black holes

text: What type of geologic fault is characterized by upward displacement of a footwall?

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of the contrails produced by air traffic: 1) They are mostly composed of water ice; 2) They have a high albedo relative to oceans and forests; 3) They form in unstable, convecting layers of the atmosphere.

Analyze the atmospheric conditions under which contrails form to assess their relationship with unstable, convecting layers.

text: Greenhouse gases build up in the atmosphere of Earth and limit the amount of heat escaping back into space. Which of the following is not a greenhouse gas for Earth?
explainAnswer: Identify the definition of greenhouse gases and their role in trapping heat in the atmosphere.

text: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding neutron stars?

Determine which statement contradicts the established facts about neutron stars.

text: The ocean floor can be mapped by altimeters [all-TIH-meh-durs] on satellites. Which of the following best describes how this method functions?

text: Which of the following statements about surface seawater salinity is true?

text: Which of the following is LEAST accurate about minerals:
choices: calcite has a hardness of 3 on most of its surfaces but a hardness of 4 along the crystal face perpendicular to its long axis
the Moh’s scale measures the absolute hardness of minerals
a mineral’s chemical composition largely determines its crystal shape and cleavage pattern
a mineral’s color is the same as its streak
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions and properties of minerals mentioned in the choices.
Evaluate each statement for accuracy based on mineralogy principles.
Determine which statement is incorrect or least accurate.
Select the choice that does not align with established mineral properties.

text: What object may be formed by the collision of two galaxies, each containing a large black hole at the core?
explainAnswer: Understand that a quasar is formed from the energy released by matter falling into a supermassive black hole.
Recognize that when two galaxies collide, their central black holes can merge.
Consider that the merging black holes can lead to increased accretion of surrounding material.
Conclude that this process can result in the formation of a quasar due to the immense energy output.

text: Identify all of the following three galaxies that are thought to have a supermassive black hole at or near their center: 1) Milky way; 2) Andromeda [ann-DRAW-meh-dah] Galaxy; 3) Whirlpool Galaxy.
explainAnswer: Research the presence of supermassive black holes in each of the listed galaxies.
Confirm that the Milky Way contains a supermassive black hole known as Sagittarius A*.
Verify that the Andromeda Galaxy is also believed to host a supermassive black hole at its center.
Check that the Whirlpool Galaxy has evidence suggesting the presence of a supermassive black hole as well.
Conclude that all three galaxies are thought to have supermassive black holes at or near their centers.

text: The Herschels proposed a model of the Milky Way that suggested that our solar system was near the center. Which of the following did they not account for in their model?
choices: The Sun's brightness only enables us to see a limited distance into the Milky Way
Their telescopes were not powerful enough to see the edge of the Milky Way
Interstellar dust obscures much of the Milky Way from our vantage point
Their sampling of stars was biased in one direction
explainAnswer: Identify the key aspects of the Herschels' model of the Milky Way.
Evaluate each choice to determine if it relates to a limitation in their model.
Consider the implications of interstellar dust on visibility and how it affects observations of the Milky Way.
Determine which option does not align with the factors the Herschels considered in their model.

text: The wet bulb of a psychrometer is used to measure which of the following properties of the atmosphere?
explainAnswer: Identify the purpose of a psychrometer, which is to measure atmospheric properties.
Understand that a psychrometer consists of two thermometers: one with a wet bulb and one with a dry bulb.
Recognize that the wet bulb thermometer measures the cooling effect of evaporation, which is related to moisture in the air.
Conclude that the measurement from the wet bulb thermometer is used to calculate humidity levels in the atmosphere.

text: What compositional layer of Earth has the steepest geothermal gradient?
explainAnswer: Understand that the geothermal gradient refers to the rate at which temperature increases with depth within the Earth.
Identify the different compositional layers of the Earth: crust, mantle, and core.
Recognize that the crust is the outermost layer and is generally cooler than the deeper layers.
Compare the geothermal gradients of the crust and other layers, noting that the crust has the steepest gradient due to its thinness and proximity to surface temperatures.
Conclude that the crust has the steepest geothermal gradient compared to the mantle and core.

text: Which of the following is NOT characteristic of currents found on the western boundary of oceanic gyres, relative to other ocean currents?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of currents on the western boundary of oceanic gyres, which are typically warm, deep, and narrow.
Compare these characteristics with the option 'slow-moving' to see if it aligns with the typical behavior of these currents.
Recognize that western boundary currents are generally fast-moving due to the Coriolis effect and other factors.
Conclude that 'slow-moving' is the only option that does not fit the characteristics of western boundary currents.

text: Ganymede is more massive than Titan, but only Titan has an atmosphere. Which of the following correctly explains this?
choices: Titan's atmosphere is mostly made of heavy gases, like sulfur dioxide, which cannot escape its gravitational pull
Titan is significantly colder than Ganymede, preventing its atmosphere from escaping
Titan actively replenishes its atmosphere, while Ganymede does not
Titan absorbs atmospheric gases from Saturn, while Ganymede does not absorb gases from Jupiter
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Identify the key factors that affect a moon's ability to retain an atmosphere, such as mass, temperature, and gravitational pull.
Compare the temperatures of Titan and Ganymede to determine how temperature influences atmospheric retention.
Recognize that lower temperatures can help retain gases by reducing their kinetic energy, making it harder for them to escape.
Conclude that Titan's significantly colder temperature compared to Ganymede is the primary reason it retains an atmosphere.

text: Identify all of the following three igneous rocks that are intrusive: 1) Gabbro; 2) Basalt; 3) Rhyolite.
explainAnswer: Understand the difference between intrusive and extrusive igneous rocks: intrusive rocks form from magma that cools slowly beneath the Earth's surface, while extrusive rocks form from lava that cools quickly on the surface.
Review the characteristics of each rock listed: Gabbro is coarse-grained and forms from slow cooling of magma, while Basalt and Rhyolite are fine-grained and form from rapid cooling of lava.
Identify that Gabbro is the only rock among the three that is classified as intrusive based on its formation process.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of augite: 1) It is an example of a pyroxene [pie-ROX-een]; 2) It has one direction of cleavage; 3) It is found in basalt.
explainAnswer: Recall that augite is a mineral classified as a pyroxene, confirming statement 1 as true.
Review the properties of augite to determine its cleavage; it actually has two directions of cleavage, making statement 2 false.
Recognize that augite is commonly found in basalt, validating statement 3 as true.

text: Which variable affecting the speed of sound in the ocean dominates at very large depths?
explainAnswer: Understand that the speed of sound in water is influenced by several factors including temperature, salinity, and pressure.
Recognize that at very large depths, the increase in water pressure becomes significant due to the weight of the water above.
Evaluate how pressure affects the density and elasticity of water, which in turn affects sound speed.
Conclude that while temperature and salinity also play roles, water pressure is the dominant factor at great depths.

text: Which of the following minerals is an industrial ore of lead and can be identified by its relative softness and three directions of cleavage?
explainAnswer: Identify the properties of the minerals listed in the choices.
Determine which mineral is known as an industrial ore of lead.
Check for the characteristic features of softness and three directions of cleavage.
Confirm that Galena matches all identified properties.

text: Meteorologists use the Enhanced Fujita Scale to determine the strength of a tornado by assessing which of the following?
choices: Minimum barometric pressure of the tornado
Damage left behind from the tornado
explainAnswer: Understand that the Enhanced Fujita Scale is specifically designed to categorize tornadoes based on their impact.
Review the choices provided and identify which one relates to the assessment of damage.
Recognize that the scale uses the damage caused to buildings and vegetation as a primary factor.
Conclude that the correct answer is the option that refers to the damage left behind from the tornado.

text: What type of mineral composes the green sand beaches that are found in the state of Hawaii?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of green sand beaches.
Research the minerals commonly found in Hawaii's geology.
Eliminate the options that are not typically associated with green sand.
Confirm that olivine is known for its green color and is a common component of green sand.

text: Which of the following provides the most accurate description of carrying capacity?
choices: Population below the carrying capacity will increase primary succession
Population above the carrying capacity cannot be sustained indefinitely
Population above the carrying capacity will always run out of space
Population above the carrying capacity will always result in excessive CO2 levels
explainAnswer: Identify the concept of carrying capacity in ecology, which refers to the maximum population size that an environment can sustain.
Evaluate each choice to see if it accurately describes the implications of exceeding carrying capacity.
Determine that the correct choice must reflect the idea that populations exceeding carrying capacity will face limitations.
Select the option that states that a population above the carrying capacity cannot be sustained indefinitely, as it directly addresses the consequences of exceeding this limit.

text: What property of diatoms make them useful as climate proxies?
choices: The chemical makeup of their shells reflects the water chemistry at their time of formation
The narrow temperature range in which they exist makes them markers for paleo0ocean temperatures
Their well-preserved digestive system provide ample evidence for ancient food webs
Their limited diversity and low adaptability make them key indicators of specific aquatic environments
explainAnswer: Identify the key characteristics of diatoms mentioned in the choices.
Evaluate how each characteristic relates to climate and environmental conditions.
Focus on the role of diatom shells in reflecting past water chemistry.
Select the choice that directly connects the chemical makeup of diatom shells to their usefulness as climate proxies.

text: Which of the following minerals is not a carbonate?
explainAnswer: Identify the chemical composition of each mineral mentioned.
Determine which of the minerals are classified as carbonates, which contain the carbonate ion (CO3)2-.
Check the composition of Fluorite, which is calcium fluoride (CaF2) and does not contain the carbonate ion.
Conclude that Fluorite is the mineral that is not a carbonate.

text: According to Bowen's reaction series, which of these minerals is the first to crystallize in cooling magma?
explainAnswer: Familiarize yourself with Bowen's reaction series, which outlines the order of mineral crystallization from cooling magma.
Identify that the series starts with the formation of olivine and progresses through various minerals.
Recognize that calcium-rich plagioclase is one of the first minerals to crystallize after olivine.
Eliminate the other choices based on their position in the series, as they crystallize at lower temperatures than calcium-rich plagioclase.

text: The northern and southern polar ice caps on Mars have a distinct carved spiral shape. Which of the following is thought to cause this shape?
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the spiral shape of the polar ice caps on Mars.
Consider the possible geological and atmospheric processes that could create such a shape.
Evaluate each option provided: wind patterns, ancient ocean currents, meteor impacts, and tectonic forces.
Determine which process is most likely to influence the surface features of Mars, particularly in relation to ice and atmosphere.
Conclude that wind patterns are the most plausible explanation for the carved spiral shape.

text: Which of the following elements most often limits primary production in freshwater lakes?
explainAnswer: Understand that primary production in aquatic ecosystems is primarily driven by nutrients.
Identify the key nutrients that influence primary production, particularly in freshwater environments.
Recognize that phosphorus is often the limiting nutrient in freshwater lakes, as it is less abundant compared to nitrogen and other nutrients.
Eliminate the other options (Oxygen, Calcium, Carbon) as they do not typically limit primary production in freshwater lakes.

text: Which of the following is closest to the top speed, in miles per hour, of a tsunami?
explainAnswer: Recall that tsunamis can travel at very high speeds in deep water.
Research indicates that the speed of a tsunami can reach up to 500 to 600 miles per hour.
Compare the provided choices to the known speed range of tsunamis.
Select the closest option to the upper limit of the tsunami speed range, which is 600 miles per hour.

text: You find a chunk of granite that you conclude, via radiometric dating, is 3.2 billion years old. The granite also contains inclusions of quartzite. Which of the following is a reasonable conclusion based on this data?
choices: The quartzite likely formed less than 3.2 billion years ago
Because the quartzite is contained in the granite, it also formed 3.2 billion years ago
The quartzite likely formed more than 3.2 billion years ago
The sandstone from which the quartzite came is likely older than 3.2 billion years, but the quartzite itself is younger than that
explainAnswer: Understand that the granite is 3.2 billion years old and serves as a host rock for the quartzite inclusions.
Recognize that inclusions are older than the rock that contains them, meaning the quartzite must have formed before the granite.
Conclude that since the granite is 3.2 billion years old, the quartzite must be older than that.
Choose the answer that states the quartzite likely formed more than 3.2 billion years ago.

text: Which of the following is NOT an example of an ichnofossil?
explainAnswer: Understand that ichnofossils are traces of biological activity, such as tracks or burrows, rather than the remains of the organisms themselves.
Identify the options given: Shell, Burrow, Coprolite, Urolite.
Recognize that a shell is a physical part of an organism, while the others are traces of behavior or activity.
Conclude that the shell is not an ichnofossil, as it is a direct fossil of the organism rather than a trace.

text: Marine sediment in the North Atlantic is primarily calcareous [kal-CARE-ee-us] ooze, while marine sediment in the North Pacific is primarily pelagic [peh-LAJ-ik] clay. Which of the following best explains why?
choices: The North Pacific has a higher pH than the North Atlantic
The North Pacific is deeper than the North Atlantic
The North Pacific has a lower pH than the North Atlantic
The North Pacific has more dissolved oxygen than the North Atlantic
explainAnswer: Understand that calcareous ooze is formed from the accumulation of calcium carbonate from organisms, which is more prevalent in higher pH conditions.
Recognize that pelagic clay is more common in areas with lower biological productivity and lower pH.
Identify that the North Pacific's lower pH leads to less calcium carbonate preservation, resulting in more clay sediment.
Eliminate other choices by considering their implications on sediment types and pH levels.

text: Which of the following is the best approximation of how much time a supergiant star can survive by way of silicon fusion? W) 1 day X) 1 year Y) 1 thousand years Y) 1 million years
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)
explainAnswer: Understand that supergiant stars have a very short lifespan due to their rapid fusion processes.
Recognize that silicon fusion occurs in the later stages of a supergiant's life.
Recall that the time frame for silicon fusion in supergiant stars is extremely brief compared to other fusion processes.
Eliminate longer time frames such as 1 year, 1 thousand years, and 1 million years based on the rapid consumption of fuel during this stage.
Conclude that the best approximation for the time a supergiant star can survive by way of silicon fusion is 1 day.

text: Which of the following is NOT true of the lunar maria?
choices: They formed within the first one billion years of the moon's history
They cover about 50% of the moon's surface
They are composed of iron-rich basalt
They are more abundant on the near side of the moon
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of lunar maria based on scientific knowledge.
Evaluate each choice against established facts about the lunar maria.
Determine which statement does not align with the known data about the lunar maria.
Select the statement that is false as the answer.

text: The Columbia River Gorge primarily cuts through what type of rock? W) Granite Y) Sandstone X) Basalt Z) Schist [SHIST]
explainAnswer: Identify the geological features of the Columbia River Gorge.
Research the predominant rock types in the region.
Determine which rock type is most commonly associated with the formation of the gorge.
Select the correct answer based on the information gathered.

text: A wind blowing from 135° equates to the wind coming from which direction?
explainAnswer: Understand that wind direction is measured from where the wind originates.
A wind coming from 135° means it is blowing towards 315° (135° + 180°).
Determine the compass direction for 315°, which is Northwest.
Since the question asks for the direction the wind is coming from, we look at the opposite direction, which is Southeast.

text: In which city would you be able to see cirrus clouds at an altitude of 3,000 meters above the surface?
explainAnswer: Understand that cirrus clouds typically form at high altitudes, usually above 6,000 meters, but can sometimes be observed at lower altitudes in certain conditions.
Consider the geographical locations and climates of the cities listed to determine where cirrus clouds are more likely to form at lower altitudes.
Recognize that Barrow, Alaska, has a colder climate which can support the formation of cirrus clouds at lower altitudes compared to warmer locations.
Eliminate the other options based on their warmer climates which are less conducive to seeing cirrus clouds at 3,000 meters.

text: What are the two main non-oxygen elements in coal combustion products that are responsible for acid rain?
explainAnswer: Recall the main components of coal and their combustion products.
Identify the elements that can lead to acid formation when coal is burned.
Recognize that nitrogen oxides (NOx) and sulfur oxides (SOx) are produced during combustion.
Conclude that nitrogen and sulfur are the primary non-oxygen elements responsible for acid rain.

text: What prominent meteor shower is active from mid-July to late- August, and is associated with Comet Swift-Tuttle?
explainAnswer: Identify the time frame mentioned in the question, which is mid-July to late-August.
Recall major meteor showers that occur during this period.
Associate the meteor shower with its parent comet, which in this case is Comet Swift-Tuttle.
Conclude that the meteor shower associated with Comet Swift-Tuttle during this time is the Perseid meteor shower.

text: Which of the seven spectral classes includes our Sun?
explainAnswer: Understand that the seven spectral classes are O, B, A, F, G, K, and M, categorized based on temperature and color of stars.
Know that the Sun is a medium-sized star and is classified based on its surface temperature and color.
Identify that the Sun's surface temperature is approximately 5,500 degrees Celsius, which corresponds to the G class.
Conclude that since the Sun fits the criteria for the G spectral class, it is classified as a G-type star.

text: Identify all of the following three processes that remove nitrogen gas from Earth's atmosphere: 1) Nitrogen fixation; 2) Denitrification; 3) Forest fires.
explainAnswer: Understand that nitrogen fixation is the process that converts nitrogen gas into a form usable by living organisms, effectively removing it from the atmosphere.
Recognize that denitrification is the process that converts nitrates back into nitrogen gas, returning it to the atmosphere, so it does not remove nitrogen gas.
Note that forest fires do not specifically target nitrogen gas removal; they primarily affect carbon and other elements.
Conclude that only nitrogen fixation is the process that removes nitrogen gas from the atmosphere.

text: Our sun produces over 90% of its energy via what specific nuclear reaction chain?
explainAnswer: Recall that the sun generates energy through nuclear fusion.
Identify the primary fusion process that occurs in stars like the sun.
Recognize that the sun primarily fuses hydrogen nuclei to form helium.
Conclude that this specific fusion process is known as the proton-proton chain.

text: Scientists can study solar fusion via observations of certain near-massless particles that travel through the Sun. What are these particles?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is about solar fusion and its byproducts.
Recall that solar fusion occurs in the Sun's core and produces various particles.
Consider the properties of particles that are near-massless and can escape the Sun's dense environment.
Recognize that neutrinos are known for their extremely small mass and ability to pass through matter almost undetected.
Conclude that the particles scientists study to observe solar fusion are indeed neutrinos.

text: Detecting signatures of gravitational waves on the cosmic microwave background would lend support to what theory first proposed by Alan Guth?
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)
explainAnswer: Identify the key concepts related to gravitational waves and the cosmic microwave background (CMB).
Recall the theory proposed by Alan Guth that relates to the early universe and rapid expansion.
Connect the detection of gravitational waves on the CMB to the implications for the theory of inflation.
Conclude that the correct answer is inflation based on the relationship between these concepts.

text: Rank the following three materials in increasing order of speed of P-waves when traveling through them: 1) Ultramafic; 2) Felsic; 3) Mafic.
explainAnswer: Understand that P-waves travel faster in denser and more rigid materials.
Recognize that felsic materials are less dense and have lower rigidity compared to mafic materials.
Identify that ultramafic materials are denser and have higher rigidity than both felsic and mafic.
Rank the materials based on their density and rigidity: felsic (lowest speed), mafic (medium speed), ultramafic (highest speed).
Conclude the order as felsic (2), mafic (3), ultramafic (1).

text: What is the empirical formula and charge of the silicon-oxygen tetrahedron, also known as the fundamental building block of all silicate materials?
explainAnswer: Identify the components of the silicon-oxygen tetrahedron, which consists of one silicon atom and four oxygen atoms.
Determine the ratio of silicon to oxygen atoms in the tetrahedron, which is 1:4.
Simplify the ratio to find the empirical formula, which represents the simplest whole number ratio of the elements.
The empirical formula for the silicon-oxygen tetrahedron is SiO, indicating one silicon atom for every one oxygen atom in the simplified form.

text: Identify all of the following three marine regions that host coral reefs: 1) The Red Sea; 2) The Australian Coast; 3) The Brazilian Coast.
explainAnswer: Research the geographical locations of coral reefs globally.
Identify the marine regions mentioned: The Red Sea, The Australian Coast, and The Brazilian Coast.
Check scientific resources or databases to confirm the presence of coral reefs in each of these regions.
Conclude that all three regions host coral reefs based on the gathered information.

text: What subsurface phenomenon, defined as soil that is perennially frozen, occurs beneath much of the state of Alaska and, as it melts, causes extensive damage of roads, trains, and pipelines?
answer: PERMAFROST (ALSO ACCEPT: PERENNIALLY CRYOTIC SOIL; DO NOT
explainAnswer: Identify the geographical location mentioned in the question, which is Alaska.
Consider the environmental conditions in Alaska, particularly those related to temperature and soil.
Recall the term that describes soil that remains frozen for extended periods, especially in cold regions.
Conclude that the phenomenon affecting infrastructure due to melting frozen soil is known as permafrost.

text: The significant drop in ozone over Antarctica, sometimes referred to as an ozone hole, is most pronounced in what Southern hemisphere season?
explainAnswer: Identify the seasons in the Southern Hemisphere: summer, autumn, winter, and spring.
Understand that the ozone layer is affected by temperature and sunlight.
Recognize that the Antarctic spring occurs from September to November.
Note that the significant drop in ozone is linked to the return of sunlight in spring, which triggers chemical reactions that deplete ozone.

text: The Kansan, Nebraskan, Illinoian, and Wisconsinan glacial events occurred in what geological epoch?
explainAnswer: Identify the glacial events mentioned in the question.
Research the time periods associated with each of these glacial events.
Determine which geological epoch encompasses all of these events.
Conclude that the Pleistocene epoch is the correct answer.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true regarding the differences between S waves and P waves: 1) P waves are longitudinal waves, while S waves are transverse waves; 2) P waves tend to have much larger amplitudes than S waves; 3) P waves travel faster than S waves.
explainAnswer: Identify the definitions of P waves and S waves, noting that P waves are longitudinal and S waves are transverse.
Evaluate the amplitude characteristics of P waves and S waves to determine if P waves have larger amplitudes.
Compare the speeds of P waves and S waves to see which travels faster.
Determine which statements are true based on the evaluations made in the previous steps.

text: The flux of energy from the Sun at Earth is about 1,000 watts per square meter. What is the solar flux, in watts per square meter, for Jupiter, which is a distance of 5 astronomical units from the Sun?
subtopic: Stellar Remnants (White Dwarfs, Neutron Stars, Black Holes)
explainAnswer: Identify that the solar flux decreases with the square of the distance from the Sun.
Use the formula for solar flux: F = F0 / d^2, where F0 is the solar flux at 1 AU (1,000 W/m^2) and d is the distance in AU.
Substitute the values into the formula: F = 1000 W/m^2 / (5^2).
Calculate the denominator: 5^2 = 25.
Divide 1000 by 25 to find the solar flux at Jupiter: 1000 W/m^2 / 25 = 40 W/m^2.

text: An alien astronomer is observing our Sun as a flat disk with a temperature of 5800 kelvins when Jupiter passes in front of it. Given that the Sun has a radius of approximately 430,000 miles and Jupiter has a radius of approximately 43,000 miles and that Jupiter contributes negligible brightness to the system, then, to one significant figure, by what percentage does the brightness of the disk drop when Jupiter passes in front of the Sun?
explainAnswer: Calculate the area of the Sun using the formula A = πr², where r is the radius of the Sun.
Calculate the area of Jupiter using the same formula with Jupiter's radius.
Determine the fraction of the Sun's area that Jupiter covers by dividing Jupiter's area by the Sun's area.
Convert this fraction into a percentage to find the percentage drop in brightness.

text: Identify all of the following three statements that are true of cosmic molecular clouds: 1) Hydrogen in molecular clouds is typically present as H<sub>2</sub>; 2) They contain trace amounts of small organic compounds such as formaldehyde; 3) Constituents of molecular clouds are typically present as ions.
explainAnswer: Evaluate each statement about cosmic molecular clouds individually.
Recall that hydrogen in molecular clouds primarily exists as H2, making the first statement true.
Consider the presence of small organic compounds like formaldehyde in molecular clouds, confirming the second statement as true.
Recognize that constituents of molecular clouds are mostly neutral molecules rather than ions, making the third statement false.
Conclude that the true statements are 1 and 2.

text: COROT [KOH-roh]was a mission run by the European Space Agency to find what type of celestial objects?
explainAnswer: Identify the organization responsible for the COROT mission, which is the European Space Agency.
Understand the primary goal of the COROT mission in the context of astronomy.
Research the types of celestial objects that are typically studied in exoplanet research.
Conclude that the COROT mission was specifically aimed at discovering exoplanets.

text: At what type of plate boundary is there no destruction or creation of lithosphere due to the relative motion being in the horizontal direction?
answer: TRANSFORM (ACCEPT: CONSERVATIVE; DO NOT ACCEPT: STRIKE-SLIP,
explainAnswer: Identify the types of plate boundaries: convergent, divergent, and transform.
Understand that convergent boundaries involve destruction of lithosphere, while divergent boundaries involve creation.
Recognize that transform boundaries involve horizontal movement without creation or destruction of lithosphere.
Conclude that the correct answer is transform, also known as conservative boundary.

text: Identify all of the following three minerals that have a single well-defined cleavage plane: 1) Pyroxene; 2) Olivine; 3) Mica.
explainAnswer: Recall the definitions of cleavage in minerals, focusing on the number of planes and their characteristics.
Review the mineral properties of Pyroxene, Olivine, and Mica regarding their cleavage.
Identify that Mica exhibits a single well-defined cleavage plane, while Pyroxene has two and Olivine has none.

text: The 21-centimeter radio emission line is due to a transition in what element?
explainAnswer: Recall that the 21-centimeter line refers to a specific wavelength of electromagnetic radiation.
Identify that this wavelength is associated with atomic transitions in hydrogen.
Understand that this transition occurs when the electron in a hydrogen atom changes its spin state.
Conclude that the element responsible for the 21-centimeter emission line is hydrogen.

text: What type of tide results when the Sun and the Moon are at right angles to each other with respect to Earth?
explainAnswer: Identify the positions of the Sun and the Moon relative to Earth.
Determine the gravitational effects of the Sun and Moon on Earth's water.
Recognize that when the Sun and Moon are at right angles, their gravitational forces partially cancel each other out.
Conclude that this results in lower high tides and higher low tides, which is characteristic of a neap tide.

text: After the first 4 billion years of Earth’s history, what relatively short evolutionary event brought forth most major animal phyla, as evidenced in the fossil record?
explainAnswer: Identify the time period in Earth's history that is known for significant evolutionary changes.
Recall the term commonly used to describe the rapid emergence of most major animal phyla.
Cross-reference this term with the fossil record to confirm its significance.
Conclude that the event is known as the Cambrian Explosion.

text: The spectra of type IA supernovae are unique because they do NOT contain lines for what element?
explainAnswer: Understand that type IA supernovae are characterized by their lack of hydrogen in their spectra.
Recall that the presence of specific elements in a supernova spectrum can indicate the type of supernova.
Identify that type IA supernovae result from the thermonuclear explosion of a white dwarf, which does not have hydrogen.
Conclude that the absence of hydrogen lines in the spectrum is a defining feature of type IA supernovae.

text: The Great Basin, Gobi, and Takla Makan are examples of what type of deserts?
explainAnswer: Identify the geographical characteristics of the Great Basin, Gobi, and Takla Makan deserts.
Research the climatic conditions that lead to the formation of these deserts.
Determine if these deserts are classified based on their location relative to mountain ranges and prevailing winds.
Conclude that these deserts are formed due to rainshadow effects, which results in their classification as rainshadow deserts.

text: What is the name of the geologic principle that states that, in an un-deformed sequence of sedimentary rocks, the youngest beds are always at the top and the oldest at the bottom?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which is related to geology and sedimentary rock formation.
Recall the fundamental principles of stratigraphy, particularly those related to the layering of rocks.
Focus on the principle that describes the vertical arrangement of sedimentary layers.
Conclude that the principle stating the youngest layers are on top and the oldest on the bottom is known as the Principle of Superposition.

text: Pahoehoe and a'a are lava flows associated with what type of magma?
explainAnswer: Identify the types of lava flows mentioned: Pahoehoe and a'a.
Recall the characteristics of these lava flows, noting that they are typically smooth and fluid versus rough and jagged.
Associate these characteristics with the type of magma that produces them.
Recognize that both Pahoehoe and a'a flows are primarily associated with basaltic magma.

text: With what type of plate boundary is the Mariana Trench associated?
explainAnswer: Identify the geological features associated with the Mariana Trench.
Recognize that the Mariana Trench is the deepest part of the ocean, formed by subduction.
Determine that subduction occurs at convergent plate boundaries where one plate moves under another.
Conclude that the type of plate boundary associated with the Mariana Trench is convergent.

text: Which of the following glacial features can result from calving?
explainAnswer: Identify what calving means in the context of glaciers, which is the process of ice breaking off from the edge of a glacier.
Consider the options provided and determine which feature is directly formed from the calving process.
Recognize that icebergs are large pieces of freshwater ice that have broken off from glaciers or ice shelves.
Eliminate the other options (drumlins, striations, moraines) as they do not result directly from calving.

text: What determines when a tropical depression or storm is given hurricane status?
explainAnswer: Understand the classification criteria for tropical systems.
Identify the specific wind speed thresholds that differentiate tropical depressions, storms, and hurricanes.
Recognize that hurricane status is specifically defined by sustained wind speeds of 74 mph or higher.
Eliminate other factors such as central pressure, diameter, and movement velocity as they do not directly determine hurricane status.

text: A barchan dune developes perpendicular to a moderate-velocity, uniform wind. Which of the following dunes is developed by variable wind direction?
explainAnswer: Understand that barchan dunes form in a consistent wind direction.
Identify that star dunes are formed in areas with variable wind directions.
Eliminate other options by recognizing that longitudinal dunes form parallel to wind, seif dunes are linear and also aligned with wind, and dome dunes are not influenced by wind direction.
Conclude that the correct answer is star dunes due to their formation from changing wind patterns.

text: Which of the following minerals is the most economically important ore for mining and extraction of the element mercury?
explainAnswer: Identify the element in question, which is mercury.
Research the common ores that contain mercury.

text: By name or number, indicate all of the following three plate boundaries that are correctly paired with fault types. 1) Convergent and normal 2) Transform and reverse 3) Divergent and thrust

text: Identify the fine-grained counterpart in the coarse-grained igneous rock diorite.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following three metamorphic rocks which exhibit foliation. 1) Slate 2) Schist 3) Quartzite

text: By name or number, identify all of the following three statements that are true of CO 2 measurements taken at Mauna Loa: 1) CO 2 concentrations peak at the end of winter 2) CO 2 concentrations have increased by more than 100% from pre-industrial levels 3) Increases in average CO 2 concentration have been roughly linear over time

text: A star has a parallax angle of 0.1 arcseconds. How far away, in parsecs, is the star from the earth?

text: A new Solar System planet is discovered to have a circular orbit and a period of 512 years. In astronomical units, how distant is the planet from the Sun?
explainAnswer: Use Kepler's Third Law, which states that the square of the orbital period (P) of a planet is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis (a) of its orbit: P^2 = a^3.
Convert the period from years to the appropriate units if necessary, but since we are using astronomical units, we can keep it in years.
Substitute the given period (512 years) into the equation: (512)^2 = a^3.
Calculate (512)^2 to get 262144, then take the cube root of 262144 to find a.
The cube root of 262144 is 64, so the planet is 64 astronomical units from the Sun.

explainAnswer: Identify the definitions and characteristics of the CNO cycle and the proton-proton chain to compare their temperature dependencies.
Research the S process and its occurrence in stellar environments, particularly in asymptotic giant branch stars.
Examine the conditions required for the triple-alpha process and the mass thresholds for its occurrence in stars.
Evaluate each statement based on the gathered information to determine which are true.

text: Which of the following objects in the solar system has the highest albedo?
explainAnswer: Understand that albedo is a measure of how much light an object reflects compared to how much it receives.

text: What term refers to a location in an ocean basin where no tidal amplitude is experienced due to the Coriolis Effect?

text: Which of the following is a possible configuration for Venus?

text: A certain galaxy has a known distance from Earth of 2.1 gigaparsecs. Using 70 kilometers per second per megaparsec as the Hubble parameter, what is the redshift? Use the special relativistic approximation and give your answer to the nearest tenth.
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)
explainAnswer: Convert the distance from gigaparsecs to megaparsecs by multiplying by 1000, resulting in 2100 megaparsecs.
Multiply the distance in megaparsecs by the Hubble parameter (70 km/s/Mpc) to find the velocity: 2100 Mpc * 70 km/s/Mpc = 147000 km/s.
Use the formula for redshift z = (v/c), where c is the speed of light (approximately 300000 km/s).
Calculate the redshift: z = 147000 km/s / 300000 km/s.
Round the result to the nearest tenth to get the final answer, which is 0.7.

text: Which of the following best explains the observational difference between Seyfert galaxies and quasar host galaxies?
choices: Quasars are usually detected in visible light, while Seyferts are usually radio sources
Quasars are generally much more luminous and further away, so that their host galaxy is not detected
Quasars have their jets oriented directly towards Earth while Seyferts have a different orientation
Quasars are in elliptical active galaxies, while Seyferts are spiral
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)

Evaluate the luminosity and distance of quasars compared to Seyfert galaxies.
Consider how distance affects the detectability of host galaxies.
Select the statement that accurately reflects the relationship between luminosity, distance, and detection of host galaxies.

text: The formation of a reservoir by damming a river or stream will have which of the following effects?
explainAnswer: Understand that damming a river creates a reservoir, which alters the flow of water.
Recognize that the water level behind the dam will rise, leading to a higher stream profile upstream.
Consider how the dam affects sediment transport, which can lead to increased deposition downstream rather than upstream.
Eliminate options that do not align with the effect of raising the water level, such as downcutting or lowering the base level.

text: What is the distance, to the nearest megaparsec, of a galaxy moving at a recessional velocity of 120 kilometers per second?
explainAnswer: Use Hubble's Law, which states that the recessional velocity (v) of a galaxy is proportional to its distance (d) from us, given by the formula v = H0 * d.
Identify the Hubble constant (H0), which is approximately 70 kilometers per second per megaparsec.
Rearrange the formula to solve for distance: d = v / H0.
Substitute the given values: d = 120 km/s / 70 km/s/Mpc.
Calculate the distance and round to the nearest megaparsec, resulting in approximately 2 Mpc.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following three statements that are true of the cosmic microwave background: 1) Its temperature is around 30 kelvin 2) It was formed at an early stage of the universe 3) It serves as evidence for the Big Bang
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of the cosmic microwave background (CMB).
Evaluate the temperature of the CMB, which is approximately 2.7 kelvin, not 30 kelvin.
Recall that the CMB was formed about 380,000 years after the Big Bang, indicating an early stage of the universe.
Recognize that the CMB provides strong evidence for the Big Bang theory.

text: Which of the following statements describes the conditions under which absolute instability would occur?
choices: Environmental lapse rate is less than the wet adiabatic rate
Environmental lapse rate is less than the dry adiabatic rate
Environmental lapse rate is greater than the wet adiabatic rate
Environmental lapse rate is greater than the dry adiabatic rate
explainAnswer: Understand that absolute instability occurs when a rising air parcel is warmer than the surrounding environment.
Recognize that the dry adiabatic rate is the rate at which unsaturated air cools as it rises.
Compare the environmental lapse rate with the dry adiabatic rate.
Conclude that if the environmental lapse rate is greater than the dry adiabatic rate, the air parcel will continue to rise, indicating absolute instability.

text: By name or number, order the following four ions in increasing concentration in seawater: 1) Sodium 2) Chloride 3) Calcium 4) Magnesium
explainAnswer: Research the average concentration of each ion in seawater.
Identify that sodium and chloride are the most abundant ions.
Note that magnesium is less abundant than sodium but more than calcium.
Rank the ions from least to most abundant based on their concentrations.

text: By name or number, order the following three cloud types by increasing altitude of where they are usually found: 1) Cirrus 2) Cumulus 3) Stratus
explainAnswer: Identify the typical altitudes at which each cloud type is found.
Stratus clouds are typically found at low altitudes.
Cumulus clouds are usually found at mid-level altitudes.
Cirrus clouds are generally found at high altitudes.
Order the cloud types from lowest to highest altitude: Stratus (3), Cumulus (2), Cirrus (1).

text: What term refers to the periods when glaciers advance extremely quickly, at rates of up to 100 times their normal speed?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which relates to glaciology and the behavior of glaciers.

text: In which of the following layers of the atmosphere does the ozone layer primarily reside in?
explainAnswer: Recall the different layers of the atmosphere: Troposphere, Stratosphere, Mesosphere, and Thermosphere.

text: What is the name of the angle which is the steepest angle where unconsolidated granulated material remains stable at a slope?

Consider the factors that influence the angle of repose, such as the size and shape of the granules and the material's cohesion.
Conclude that the term you are looking for is the angle of repose.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following three planets which generate internal heat from the Kelvin-Helmholtz mechanism: 1) Uranus 2) Saturn 3) Jupiter
explainAnswer: Understand that the Kelvin-Helmholtz mechanism involves the gradual contraction of a planet, which generates internal heat.

text: Which of the following is closest to the critical density of the universe in kilograms per meter cubed?
subtopic: Cosmology (Big Bang, CMB, expansion of universe)
explainAnswer: Understand that critical density is the density at which the universe is flat.

text: What term describes the thin strands of glass that form from the solidification of thin strands of lava after a basaltic eruption?
explainAnswer: Identify the context of the question, which involves volcanic activity and basaltic eruptions.

text: The Blandford-Znajeck (BLAN-ford-ZNAHjeck) process is a proposed mechanism for the extraction of energy from a rotating black hole with a strong magnetic field. explainAnswer: Understand the Blandford-Znajek process and its relation to rotating black holes and magnetic fields.
Identify the characteristics of astrophysical jets and how they relate to energy extraction from black holes.
Evaluate active galactic nuclei and their connection to black holes and energy emission.

Conclude that only astrophysical jets and active galactic nuclei are explained by the Blandford-Znajek process.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following three locations in a galaxy that one would predominately expect to find Population 1 stars: 1) Halo 2) Spiral arms 3) Galactic disk
explainAnswer: Understand that Population 1 stars are young, metal-rich stars typically found in regions with active star formation.
Identify that spiral arms are regions in a galaxy where stars, gas, and dust are concentrated, making them likely locations for Population 1 stars.
Recognize that the galactic disk is the flat, rotating part of a galaxy that contains most of its young stars, including Population 1 stars.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following three statements that are true about the Bergeron process: 1) It involves supercooled water freezing upon impact with a solid surface 2) Forming ice crystals absorb water vapor as they grow 3) Only snow and not rain can be caused by the Bergeron Process
explainAnswer: Evaluate each statement individually to determine its accuracy regarding the Bergeron process.

Recognize that ice crystals can grow by absorbing water vapor, confirming the truth of statement 2.
Identify that the Bergeron process can lead to both snow and rain, making statement 3 false.

text: When the swash of a wave approaches the shoreline in an oblique fashion and the backwash is then parallel to the shore what phenomenon occurs?
explainAnswer: Identify the movement of the wave as it approaches the shore, noting its oblique angle.

Understand that the difference in direction between the swash and backwash leads to sediment being transported along the shore.

text: By name or number, identify all of the following three currents that are cold water currents: 1) California Current 2) Labrador Current 3) Gulf Stream
explainAnswer: Identify the characteristics of cold water currents, which typically originate from polar regions and flow towards the equator.

text: The COBE (KOH-bee) probe accurately measured the near-perfect black body spectrum of what phenomenon?

text: What class of eclipsing binaries, named after a Perseus star, is semidetached and has a star whose Roche lobe is unfilled?

text: By name or number, identify all of the following four moons that are satellites of Saturn: 1) Enceladus 2) Ganymede 3) Triton 4) Miranda

text: A star has a temperature 5 times that of the sun and a radius 2 times that of the sun. The luminosity of this star is how many times greater than the solar luminosity?

text: By name or number, identify all of the following three minerals that are cyclosilicates: 1) Beryl 2) Tourmaline (TORE-muh-leen) 3) Topaz

text: By name or number, identify all of the following three objects that would be relatively absent from elliptical galaxies: 1) RR Lyrae variables 2) Giant molecular clouds 3) Herbig-Haro objects

text: By name or number, identify all of the following four rocks or minerals that could contain the majority of the iron content of the iron rich layers found in banded iron formations: 1) Hematite (HEE-muh-tite) 2) Magnetite 3) Chert 4) Siderite (SID-uh-rite)

text: Which of the following statements explains why superior mirages are more prevalent over water bodies or icy surfaces?
choices: Air closer to the ground needs to be colder
Air closer to the ground needs to be warmer
Air closer to the ground needs to be less humid
Air closer to the ground needs to be more humid

text: A lake in Illinois is approximately 9 feet deep. By name or number, identify all of the following four processes that it is likely to undergo: 1) Fall turnover 2) Winter stratification 3) Spring turnover 4) Summer stratification
explainAnswer: Understand that lakes experience seasonal changes in temperature and density, leading to stratification and turnover processes.

text: What process allows for Strömgren (STRAWMgruhn) spheres to maintain a constant radius when in equilibrium with ionizing photons?

text: By name or number, identify all of the following three statements that correctly describe a difference between gegenschein (GAY-gen-shine) and zodiacal (zoh-DYE-uh-kuhl) light: 1) It has a low angle of reflection of the incident sunlight on dust particles 2) It forms a dimmer elliptical spot within the brighter part of zodiacal light 3) Dust particles for zodiacal light are seen in full phase
